title: RBD upstream updates
author: yehudasa
content: qemu-rbd qemu-rbd block device been merged upstream into qemu project qemu-rbd created originally by christian brunner binary compatible with linux native rbd driver allows creation qemu block devices that are striped over objects rados — ceph distributed object store with corresponding linux device driver qemu driver gets all rbd goodies thin provisioning reliability scalability snapshots libvirt libvirt virtualization library that allows controlling virtual machines such qemu based vms also others using single api there are many tools already built around e g virsh virt-manager etc adding ability configure rbd devices via library makes rbd work existing tools with help sheepdog project whom also merged their qemu block device upstream into qemu recently were able get rbd sheepdog also nbd support upstream into libvirt basically new network disk type added there are currently 3 possible types such disk nbd sheepdog rbd each can specify host name e g rbd host name would hold ip address tcp port ceph cluster monitor libvirt support linux native kernel rbd driver also works which will allow rbd used with non-qemu vms supported by libvirt e g xen virtualbox vmware etc more information about using qemu-rbd libvirt see http ceph newdream net wiki qemu-rbd linux kernel posted before rbd native linux device merged into upcoming linux kernel version 2 6 37 which will out few weeks since original merge modified rbd sysfs interface that d conform better with sysfs requirements originally rbd driver based another linux block device called osdblk inherited its sysfs interface which monolithic kept single sysfs entry per config option all devices this both wrong cumbersome needed specify device id each operation new interface moves sysfs rbd subdir better location sys bus rbd creates subdir per device that all operations single device are grouped together there need specify device name also create subdir per snapshot under device that holds all its information dropped one-big-list- -all entry all all relatively big change introduce well into release cycle believe worth

title: Ceph Comes to Synnefo and Ganeti
author: scuttlemonkey
content: during most recent schlep through europe met some really great people heard some awesome ceph use cases one particularly interesting case work guys synnefo shared with fosdem that they have been doing with ganeti rados they were nice enough write some details their blog give permission repost here any have interesting things that have done with ceph always want hear about feel free send link ceph email our community alias now goods synnefo rados lt 3 are happy announce that synnefo now supports completely unified storage files images vm disks over commodity hardware using rados since passed testing phase now heading our production environment okeanos scales what does completely unified storage mean why rados let take things from beginning problem 1 trying scale public cloud service over commodity hardware trivial task first mid 2011 had all our vms running over drbd with ganeti our file object storage service pithos backed by big nas drbd great production-quality software enabling live migrations with shared storage aggregate bandwidth that scales with number compute nodes wanted keep all that other hand knew that wanted storage service scale had get rid nas title: CephFS MDS Status Discussion
author: gfarnum
content: there have been lot questions lately about current status ceph mds when expect stable release inktank been having some internal discussions around cephfs release development d like share them with ask feedback couple quick notes first this blog post from perspective inktank development aren t only ones generating metadata server mds patches other parties might make contributions with different priorities second this discussion about mds development — look blog about what mds does how works coming soon current status over past year inktank have regretfully stepped back from filesystem — still believe its feature set capabilities will revolutionize storage realized required lot more work become stable product than rbd rgw focused our efforts software could give customers that still inktank organizational focus turn year something wonderful personally happened created internal cephfs team sam lang have been devoting increasing amount our time work mds filesystem development this renewed focus emphasized what kinds issues remain there are few brave organizations using cephfs testing production capacities more important its use them less functionality they rely community members recommendation been test cephfs under your workload two weeks inject some failures node restarts etc works through that then should continue working — some people have run systems months without issues others run into trouble their second third command basically your workload happens look like one test suites regularly run should good — deviates even little there are hidden traps lying wait from bugs that haven t yet discovered initially our goal stabilize features filesystem already develop fsck through recent discussions realized hadn t sat down figured out what our users customers actually needed cephfs order put into production deployments more than that while viewed cephfs years this big ball awesomeness with features like snapshotting multiple active servers unlimited directory sizes don t know which those features are actually necessary first release — bugs been working have reminded us that some them require lot more stability work than others keeping that thought mind now starting discussion with customers users community large discuss what minimum viable product cephfs would look like our starting point just what easy from development perspective would welcome feedback from users this works them how would need change before they could deploy minimum viable product proposal put more engineering resources back into cephfs are looking what would consider minimal useful feature set order get cephfs into hands production users soon possible are currently considering single active mds with maximum number entries single directory fsck snapshots this delivers posix-compliant filesystem that can mounted thousands clients scales arbitrarily large data throughputs allows unlimited number files hierarchy location-aware can used through number interfaces ganesha nfs hadoop -kernel fuse-based clients samba etc let break down what each those assertions means more detail single active mds one cephfs flagship features its horizontal scalability across very large numbers metadata server daemons this will continue flagship feature future right now introduces significant system instability will part our initial supported release however standby active standby features are very stable will part first release this means that fast failover features 30 seconds much less depending user settings hardware tolerance unnecessary failovers will function allowing users provision many servers they wish case hardware failure take over during maintenance primary limits implied by single-mds configuration are number metadata operations second system can handle number simultaneous client connections can handle amount metadata mds can store memory this last provides limit how many files can use simultaneously with good performance total number files system which remains effectively unlimited always amount ram cpu available mds node will have dramatic impact where precisely these limits fall aside currently default 100 000 inodes cache that extremely conservative fits inside low hundreds mb ram don t yet have recent specific values memory consumption per inode maximum number entries single directory cephfs includes preliminary support directory fragmenting sharding which allows us both split single directory -disk split between multiple mds servers again though while code exists requires significant amount validation debugging our first release will provide support will need limit total number entries allowed within single directory this soft limit open negotiation — mds needs able hold whole directory -memory whenever read disk directory holds more entries than mds cache can hold cache efficiency overall performance will naturally degrade more than one directory use they will feed back each other however manually sharding directories by splitting them according any given heuristic which splits them finely enough works just fine this limit does imply limit total number files system long one considers maximum amount active metadata discussed above fsck with many distributed systems cephfs does currently provide fsck initial design work been done yet implemented cephfs does course inherit rados underlying reliability methods which include periodic scrub data consistency between replicas checksum-based validity checks upcoming cuttlefish release replication data recovery when degrades unfortunately this does completely insure cephfs — objects which are completely lost will translate into file holes will necessarily trigger alarms any lost directories filesystem hierarchy which will detected must repaired manually positive side due ceph design any portions hierarchy which have been damaged will continue function even data been lost snapshots while cephfs preliminary support snapshots directory hierarchies too requires significant hardening debugging will support them our initial release when they are released will pioneering feature among distributed filesystems posix-compliant cephfs posix-compliant always been always will provides proper consistency rather than open- close nfs does supports even less commonly-used features such file locking hard links are also supported although their current implementation each link requires small bit mds memory there implied limit based your available memory have designed implemented new solution avoid this problem can used by thousands clients simultaneously past testing during sage weil phd thesis work mds servers have had trouble handling 1000 clients each while haven t tested recently expect that number have improved rather than degraded scales arbitrary data throughputs cephfs once client opened file mds does play further role data path that means that your clients can send data your osds can write data single-mds limit will directly impact aggregate bandwidth available implied limits are those based how much each client can send out total number active files mds can handle allows unlimited number will have hard limit total number files available location aware cephfs built rados which failure domain-based layout engine which by default naturally maps onto physical host rack row room layouts content: since its inception ceph always had fast-paced rolling release tempo however with amount adoption that ceph had over last year including continued integration work with several other open source projects wanted move more reliable predictable release schedule release schedule can divided into four different flavors point releases development interim releases stable releases long term support lts releases can expect these releases appears following periodic schedule point releases — ad hoc interim releases — every 2 weeks stable releases — every 3 months lts releases — coming soon point releases point releases are generated ad hoc basis purposes critical bug security fixes currently only generate point releases stable releases period 3-6 months though this may become longer certain versions included downstream distros since they are only generated -needed basis they will commicated via all blog mailing list social media channels appropriate interim releases every two weeks approximately can expect latest development work aggregated made available community wanted very aggressive schedule here make sure that everyone building things with associated with ceph had access latest greatest work by core ceph developers primarily what will see these releases will bug fixes patches smaller feature additions larger features may appear interim release however that feature should considered production ready until next stable release these announcements will appear blog ceph-devel mailing list with release number summary changes keep your eyes peeled stable releases given amount work that gone into testing qa procedures stable releases can done much more reliable frequent basis much this work been directed our primary testing tool teuthology originally written test nightlies kind tool been updated run installations task run longer term testing instead just compile-type tests include more distro-specific testing allow wider range testing parameters given amount crossover between inktank ceph development also worth noting that inktank testing lab grown from 160-ish machines around 286 machines that plus amount rigorous testing see from ceph community means that releases will put through lot more paces considered stable will have more traditional feature freeze qa period release candidate lifecycle dates this lifecycle should available soon via new ceph wiki give upstream users more visibility stable releases will include larger feature changes bug fixes stability from much more exhaustive testing these releases will function roll all interim releases since last stable version where new features that have been added can considered production-ready these releases will featured our blog mailing lists well being featured ceph com our downloads resource section each stable release will have name associated with different type cephalopod corresponding appropriate letter release stable releases thusfar argonaut bobtail lts releases given pace development incredibly wide-range use cases ceph being thrown especially amount change cephfs portion ceph don t feel that having lts releases quite makes sense yet however all work above laying very solid groundwork us make lts guarantees very near future course able get there even faster with your help getting involved more testing bug reports see from community more sure that all angles possible are being considered tested sooner able start making even more guarantees than now great example this would relatively new committer loic dachary who done bunch great work around building out unit tests love when new users show become prolific would love help anyone interested contributing succeed there are number different ways that users can get involved from writing code just running test cluster latest- -greatest code everything between are interested lending hand feel free drop us note via our mailing lists irc conclusion while this may seem like minor news quite excited by ramifications what this means ceph are very happy with how production clusters have been performing want ensure that all our users from vast enterprise deployments down single 5-minute quickstart are able expect high degree stability reliability going forward level community support testing development been amazing also would like thank all our contributors testers users title: ViPR: A software-defined storage mullet?
author: nwl
content: almost every few weeks new storage products are announced by competitors generally avoid commenting them emc vipr announcement contains attempts perform both marketing technical sleight hand around software-defined storage that potentially much slow down inevitable change that coming storage market while emc remain impressive company with record adjusting market -invention they have adopted unfortunate habit sprinkling open software-defined storage over their new product hope convincing customers that vipr something new revolutionary while vipr looks present modern interface administrator still interacts with mixture expensive ill-fitting components back others words something storage mullet complex solution parts united around vendor-controlled api control plane barest association with what open software-defined storage really mean why they are valuable business vendor open vs really open fifteen years ago data center awash mix proprietary hardware proprietary software open-source transformed this by giving users power control adapt software their own needs allowing them optimize performance their environments while driving costs down same time linux mysql apache spearheaded this shift now hadoop nosql movement are delivering even more innovation storage been one last bastions withstand this transformation which why inktank believes time right truly open-source storage system open apis are important this just about control plane offering ability integrate with other vendors systems about bringing benefits collaboration around shared problems rapid feature development entire storage stack even more about ensuring customers are locked into single vendor with move cloud infrastructure speeding innovation cycle mystery most popular cloud platforms such openstack cloudstack are all open-source vendor independent customers now want open-source throughout both compute storage layer api tied single vendor still presents risk lock- software-defined vs software-managed emc are calling vipr first software-defined storage platform only this first barely qualifies calling itself software-defined storage platform all like cloud everyone their own slightly different definition what software-defined storage means its heart intimately linked separation software functions from underlying hardware allowing customers use low-cost commodity hardware their own choosing without sacrificing features vipr better described software-managed storage principally means people integrate their existing legacy storage solutions into single control layer through which provision deploy storage pools while api layer does allow integration with modern components indeed can deploy data ceph cluster using openstack swift api adaptor still leaves bulk storage functionality locked proprietary appliances that dominate enterprise cost savings there its being first well ceph been running production multiple sites many years before last week announcement right side history emc announcement shows that they are having react shift that going towards customers using low-cost commodity hardware that excessive margin proprietary appliances sustainable also shows recognition that future storage going delivered via software apis inktank are building business that completely embraces this change flattering that emc now share our vision however vipr represents hedged rather predictable product that sees emc wanting more protect existing revenues than embrace future inktank established drive change storage industry create situation where customers pay less better enterprise customer today who comfortable using open-source technology throughout data center can longer sold more more by legacy vendors businesses are now ready genuine change how they deploy storage matter many times use words like open api software-defined customers can tell fresh choice from old story

title: v0.67 Dumpling released
author: sage
content: another three months have gone by next stable release ceph ready dumpling thank everyone who contributed this release 42 authors all this release focuses few major themes since v0 61 cuttlefish rgw global namespace region support s3 swift object storage new restful api endpoint administering cluster based new improved management api updated cli mon stability performance osd stability performance cephfs open-by-ino support improved nfs reexport improved support red hat platforms use intel crc32c instruction when available with previous stable releases can upgrade from previous versions ceph without taking entire cluster online long few simple guidelines are followed dumpling have tested upgrades from both bobtail cuttlefish are running argonaut please upgrade bobtail then dumpling please upgrade daemons hosts following order upgrade ceph-common all nodes that will use command line ceph utility upgrade all monitors upgrade ceph package restart ceph-mon daemons this can happen one daemon host time note that because cuttlefish dumpling monitors can t talk each other all monitors should upgraded relatively short succession minimize risk that untimely failure will reduce availability upgrade all osds upgrade ceph package restart ceph-osd daemons this can happen one daemon host time upgrade radosgw upgrade radosgw package restart radosgw daemons there are several small compatibility changes between cuttlefish dumpling particularly with cli interface please see complete release notes summary changes since v0 66 v0 61 cuttlefish other possible issues that should considered before upgrading dumpling second ceph release our new three-month stable release cycle are very pleased have pulled everything together schedule next stable release which will code-named emperor slated three months from now beginning november can download v0 67 dumpling from usual locations git git github com ceph ceph git tarball http ceph com download ceph-0 67 tar gz debian ubuntu packages see http ceph com docs master install debian rpms see http ceph com docs master install rpm

title: Ceph Dumpling
author: nwl
content: ceph community just finished its latest three-month cycle development culminating new major release ceph called dumpling v0 67 those more serious demeanor inktank proud have contributed two major pieces functionality dumpling 1 global namespace region support – many service providers departments want deploy object storage using region zone concepts familiar users amazon web services this release s3 swift api compatible ceph object gateway been extended enable this capability organizations using ceph can now have multiple geographically dispersed gateways connected together into single logical system with single global namespace users can then choose from multiple zones per region place multiple copies same object different physical locations resiliency this new eventually-consistent connected architecture also serves foundation additional features multi-site storage that are coming soon ceph roadmap next release entire zone will able copied separate data centers this enables only implementation disaster recovery architectures also read-affinity based policies guide users nearest available copy their data only just missed getting this feature into dumpling release are working get external agents that power copying data between clusters out next few weeks 2 ceph rest api monitoring management functions relating ceph storage cluster itself rados while software-defined storage multiple meanings inktank having programmatically driven architecture core new api means that administrators can now easily hook ceph into their existing monitoring management systems really interested see what integrations ceph community can now build through api ceph block storage rbd side were excited see external projects continuing integrate ceph into their cloud solutions citrix released tech preview their xenserver hypervisor product with support rbd full release slated later year documentation also provided red hat new community openstack distribution – rdo also showing how use rbd part rhel-based deployment finally full support rbd merged into code base upcoming apache cloudstack 4 2 release by joint-community member wido den hollander really proud ceph dumpling invite users developers join us irc ceph oftc ceph-devel ceph-user mailing lists share their feedback can also join our dumpling webinar september 5th learn more

title: Distributed storage and thinking inside the box
author: sage
content: usually try ignore all silly things that people say internet every once while there something from reputable source that sufficiently misleading that feel obliged respond cloudscaling ceo randy bias whitepaper converged storage wishful thinking amp reality example sort paper that deserves proper rebuttal only because comes from someone who normally provides keen observations interesting perspectives jeff darcy glusterfs already posted frank response summarizing his problems with randy reasoning his signature style there are few things d like highlight here first before addressing any actual arguments randy tries set some context his argument by mapping traditional storage use-cases traditional environments cloud mapping makes little sense randy quot tiered storage cloud era quot chart equates performance requirements traditional environments onto storage apis cloud performance requirements dictate apis these are completely orthogonal concepts conventional san nas products provide block file apis that can crazy fast dog slow distributed cloud solutions whether they are block object file have same range capabilities depending what technologies they are built s3 happens both low-performance weakly-consistent object store one implementation that follows decade academic research object storage whole point -called software defined storage that are longer hostage appliance vendors choice what components software wrap their tin can build object file block solutions with performance characteristics determined by whatever hardware meets your requirements any case randy offers three arguments against distributed storage systems like ceph glusterfs sheepdog let start with first two economics single technology ssd disk tape will span entire gamut cost performance requirements from tier 1 tier 3 storage technologies sometimes people need ssds high iops sometimes they need spinning disks sometimes they even gasp need tape sometimes can build hybrid systems these statements are obviously true clear what that with distributed storage solutions can buy both proprietary open systems that use different combinations ssds hdds more importantly more directly randy presumed point can build single ceph cluster that incorporates all these technologies various combinations provide different storage pools different purposes this lets capture diversity requirements performance storage apis single cluster without being confined by archaic notion that example use object api implies low performance weak consistency application wants high performance strongly consistent object storage create ceph pool using ssds use librados application bulk log storage with low performance build ceph pool with sata disks use cephfs rbd build with commodity hardware from whatever vendor happen like time manage all single cluster irony here that systems that cloudscaling appears defend are doing exactly same thing modern sans are also distributed systems with designs based many same principles algorithms that ceph glusterfs difference that they target limited size simplify scaling requirements usually 10s nodes most are forced architect around standardized legacy protocols are neatly wrapped tin with invoice service contract taped front this black box approach what creates illusion value secret sauce that allows appliance vendors charge what they what amounts commodity components proprieatary software custom nameplates also seems sufficient obscure fact that they exist same reality systems that cloudscaling fears will somehow make harder prevent from using right tool job reality that choice vendors technologies that ceph others provide gives greater flexibility storage cloud build can combine them all into single cloud boot finally third argument some background cap then therefore distributed storage systems solve scale-out problem they don t solve failure domain problem instead they make failure domain much larger idea that systems like ceph glusterfs don t allow control size failures domains profoundly misunderstands what these virtually any other distributed systems are all about failure response fact our primary preoccupation ceph case example our data distribution mechanism crush explicitly empowers system designers administrators control size layout failure domains describe data placement policies terms them one might choose replicate across hosts racks data centers depending network resiliency application requirements similarly ceph monitor daemons provide central source consensus using paxos effectively arbitrate kinds network partitions randy worried about without requiring complexity overhead paxos-like semantics data path looking cloudscaling doomsday failure example cap quot gotcha quot starters few people would build this sort 2-node 2-cluster system call distributed failure consistency semantics are marginal this degenerate case same reasons by way that pure 2-way replication with systems like drdb are fragile however assuming moment that did want build above competent ceph administrator would place single monitor third location perhaps colocated with vms utilizing storage provide reliable consensus when left sub-cluster went offline maintain both consistency availability above failure scenario behold cp system that remains available when just under half overall system out lunch more realistic sensible deployment might decide that appropriate failure domain rack group racks due shared power circuit pdu shared top rack switches etc distributed storage system would replicate across hosts within rack near-line fail-with- -user storage option much like -called ebs he advocates replicate across racks persist-across-failures storage option more like amazon s3 even replicate across data centers geographies persist-across-catastrophies solution might this all within same cluster with range pools providing different performance profiles apis based application requirements randy right that there are trade-offs here misses point that new crop distributed storage technologies are there empower make those hard choices some applications ap system might more appropriate although argue that generally dictated by application requirements that are performance-related something like swift might ideal choice restful object storage example consumers block file apis generally require strong consistency will have range availability requirements that dictate how failure domains are defined their application some users will need storage that survives only disk failures others will require consistent operation even presence entire data centers going offline like all powerful tools ceph glusterfs can misused naively throwing cloud-scale storage solution any problem can dangerous great thing about these systems that can architect storage solutions that will satisfy all these use-cases armed with basic understanding your requirements distributed consensus title: Ceph and Swift: Why we are not fighting.
author: syndicated
content: have just come back from openstack summit hong kong always blast talking lot people listening presentations designing future software all love while chatting with different people there recurrent question coming people wanted know whether ceph better than swift having been involved swift since 2008 way before openstack even idea now core developer answer obviously biased can understand when there better alternative product people are moving this normal evolution have technologies remember when back days beginning linux stubbornly wanted keep use linux terminal with lynx tools avoiding x11 because didn t see merit now happily using mac os x ceph swift are actually competing with each other they are two different technologies each with different purpose there some feature overlap between both two have different use-cases can actually live happily together same deployment features comparisons from high level perspective main differences between two object storage technologies are ceph started 2006 written c strongly consistent block storage object storage swift started 2008 written python eventually consistent object storage production really large public clouds ceph doing lot more than just object storage using open source block storage way provide remote virtual disks what people would start get attracted by does this brilliantly since seems become very popular block storage system option openstack deployments that win openstack open source community general reason ceph can block storage because being strongly consistent ensuring that everything are writing written disks before are sending ok back client being written c makes ceph very optimized performances thanks way designed allows clients talking straight storage servers osds shared file system feature work progress completely ready production just yet when will should solve really hard complex problem that people have been trying tackle last few decades swift other hand does one thing does well its only ambition object storage provide rest api access eventually consistent this means that when hardware fails which inevitable cluster swift will fall back providing high availability data swift eventual consistency window most likely seen when reading objects that were overwritten while hardware failed when looking container listings when many objects that container are created same time this eventual consistency also allows swift cluster deployed across wide geographic areas this isn t just replay logs style replication allows deployers configure cluster synchronous asynchronous replication into different distinct regions swift proxy servers are aware which region they are this allows deployers optimize throughput dispersion when new data written having python huge advantage deployers just because language itself because arguably more approachable with flexible middleware that can plug into wsgi pipeline also easy have swift plug whole lot different auth systems have all sort middleware modifying its behavior integrating specific feature like python swift philosophy being batteries included have all sorts middleware doing different thing making credible alternative s3 one final advantage swift being proven production very large scale with lot different public cloud running already like rackspace hp cloudwatt mercadolibre etc are happy with other hand way ceph does object storage via its rados gateway while being api agnostic have strong s3 emulation api powerful full scaled python wsgi system does allow modularity issue having gateway always have mimic follow swift api while core api well defined stable backward compatible that doesn t include all middleware shipped with swift use cases had choose only one had requirement block storage definitely want go with ceph had only object storage use case then would advise go with swift having said that there are use cases where want have both some organisations don t want have manage two different clusters with different systems radosgw can good enough some simple use cases want use with s3 api swift api would provide fully featured object storage system one other point take consideration that objects stored from radosgw will accessible from block storage system since they have difference usage pattern they would have placed via ceph intelligent modular placement different hardware setup end day users want have choices thanks red hat gluster team swift now multi backend system where can have different storage backend system swift which effectively would allow have ceph plugged object servers are totally there yet swift ceph developers had chats together trying see how this can plug end this would provide choices end user with minimal management conclusion don t think swift ceph rivals both are great opensource projects with specific set tasks mind main competition are proprietary software solutions resulting vendor lock- both swift ceph with their strong communities lively discussions are great solutions vast majority challenges thanks friends swiftstack rackspace inktank colleagues reviewing this post

title: Inktank Ceph Enterprise 1.2 arrives with erasure coding and cache-tiering
author: nwl
content: today proud announce availability red hat inktank ceph enterprise 1 2 solution based firefly release from ceph community this latest version brings some major new features enterprises – ones believe will both further cement ceph position leading storage solution openstack infrastructure while promoting its adoption among enterprises looking manage explosion unstructured data first major new feature red hat inktank ceph enterprise 1 2 erasure coding data-durability feature object storage erasure coding can substantially lower cost per gigabyte storing large volumes data because contrast storing replicas with high overhead erasure coding can achieve same high level protection against hardware failures while storing less data cluster erasure coding particularly well suited storing large amounts write-once read-infrequently data where performance less critical than cost second new feature red hat inktank ceph enterprise 1 2 cache tiering feature that can used either boost performance ceph block device openstack users complement erasure coding provide fast hot tier that hosts active data faster media like ssds cache tiering allows customers define cost- -performance characteristics individual data sets automatically migrate data between hot cold tiers based demand with more more data having long tail being able migrate data dynamically this way now essential when managing large data sets addition erasure coding cache tiering new red hat inktank ceph enterprise 1 2 product includes latest version newly open-source calamari ceph management platform that now adds cluster management its monitoring capabilities with this latest version calamari users can define storage pools set cluster settings initiate changes running processes response logs notifications generated by monitoring dashboard delivered one convenient installation package with needed dependencies red hat inktank ceph enterprise 1 2 available red hat enterprise linux ubuntu centos comes with full sla-backed support services excited about interest red hat inktank ceph enterprise generated opportunities believe offers our customers learn more attend our webinar wednesday july 30 look toward our future product releases confident that time come software-defined storage fundamentally change storage landscape

title: Ceph make -j8 check in less than 3mn
author: loic
content: ceph sources contain tests that can run with make check v0 85 then can only run sequentially because some tests bind same ports use same files takes around 18 minutes spinner 12 minutes ssd because some o intensive ones becomes problematic because long time wait when adding code trying validate works also because keeps increasing more tests are added also recurring frustration because they conflict with vstart sh cluster running manual testing tests have been reworked ensure that none them use same port same files reduces time 12mn spinner around 2mn ssd with make -j8 check loic rex001 src time make -j8 check make 4 entering directory home loic ceph src check version git version make 1 leaving directory home loic ceph src real 2m21 907s user 5m45 958s sys 1m50 431s number tests such qa workunits cephtool test sh take long time require much cpu disk o when 4 core machine setting -j8 gives chance these tests run while more cpu intensive tests are using most cpu power using larger values instance -j16 does help much because few tests take around 3mn run anyway

title: v0.87 Giant released
author: sage
content: this release will form basis stable release giant v0 87 x highlights giant include rados performance range improvements have been made osd client-side librados code that improve throughput flash backends improve parallelism scaling fast machines cephfs have fixed raft bugs cephfs built some basic journal recovery diagnostic tools stability performance single-mds systems vastly improved giant although yet recommend cephfs production deployments encourage testing non-critical workloads that can better guage feature usability performance stability gaps local recovery codes osds now support erasure-coding scheme that stores some additional data blocks reduce io required recover from single osd failures degraded vs misplaced ceph health reports from ceph - related commands now make distinction between data that degraded there are fewer than desired number copies data that misplaced stored wrong location cluster distinction important because latter does compromise data safety tiering improvements have made several improvements cache tiering implementation that improve performance most notably objects are promoted into cache tier by single read they must found sufficiently hot before that happens monitor performance monitors now perform writes local data store asynchronously improving overall responsiveness recovery tools ceph objectstore tool greatly expanded allow manipulation individual osds data store debugging repair purposes this most heavily used by our qa infrastructure exercise recovery code upgrade sequencing your existing cluster running version older than v0 80 x firefly please first upgrade latest firefly release before moving giant have tested upgrades directly from emperor dumpling older releases have tested firefly giant dumpling firefly giant please upgrade daemons following order monitors osds mdss radosgw note that relative ordering osds monitors should matter primarily tested upgrading monitors first upgrading from v0 80x firefly client-side caching librbd now enabled by default rbd cache true safety option rbd cache writethrough until flush true also enabled that writeback caching used until library observes flush command indicating that librbd users passing that operation through from guest vm this avoids potential data loss when used with older versions qemu that support flush leveldb write buffer size 32 title: The Ceph and TCMalloc performance story
author: shan
content: this article simply relays some recent discovery made around ceph performance finding behind this story one biggest improvement ceph performance that been seen years will just highlight summarize study case want read entirely story spring 2015 two sandisk employees named somnath roy chaitanya huilgol investigated reported issue with version tcmalloc being distributed many recent releases major linux distributions under heavy multi-threaded memory allocation workloads tcmalloc can consume significant amounts cpu when doesn t have enough thread cache available there setting that allows user increase amount thread cache beyond default 32mb though due bug this settings ignored until 2 2 releases gperftools which have yet been packaged sandisk along with several other community members provided initial ceph benchmarks showing performance benefits when using jemalloc newer tcmalloc with higher thread cache values recently 2015 ceph hackathon jian zhang from intel presented further results showing 4 7x increase iops performance when using jemalloc rather than older version tcmalloc this provided red hat with perfect opportunity replicate sandisk intel findings ceph hackathon using new performance test cluster donated ceph community by intel what observed under small io workloads jemalloc roughly 4 21x faster than tcmalloc 2 1 4kb random writes while jemalloc produced best 4kb random write performance all configurations that were tested also consumed most memory estimated that each osd jemalloc consumming additional 300mb rss 600mb virt memory latency data recorded by fio every test though only 4k random write random read results were graphed these tests 512 concurrent ios were issued from 16 fio processes 2 per node write case this resulted additional concurrency due journal writes 3x replication write case over 50 ios took 20-50ms complete when using tcmalloc 2 1 when jemalloc used over 87 ios completed 10ms less tcmalloc 2 4 with 128mb thread cache showed similar average improvement with wider overall spread when jemalloc used 4k random read test ceph able process 98 ios 2ms less while this yet sub millisecond latency much closer than what could obtained through tcmalloc even with 128mb thread cache want read entire report available here mark nelson also discussed this subject during last ceph tech talk

title: Important security notice regarding signing key and binary downloads of Ceph
author: sage
content: last week red hat investigated intrusion sites both ceph community project ceph com inktank download inktank com which were hosted computer system outside red hat infrastructure ceph com provided ceph community versions downloads signed with ceph signing key id 7ebfdd5d17ed316d download inktank com provided releases red hat ceph product ubuntu centos operating systems signed with inktank signing key id 5438c7019dceeead while investigation into intrusion ongoing our initial focus integrity software distribution channel both sites date our investigation discovered any compromised code binaries available download these sites however cannot fully rule out possibility that some compromised code binaries were available download some point past further can longer trust integrity ceph signing key therefore have created new signing key id e84ac2c0460f3994 verifying downloads this new key committed ceph git repository also available from https git ceph com release asc all future release git tags will signed with this new key this intrusion did affect other ceph sites such download ceph com which contained some ceph downloads git ceph com which mirrors various source repositories known have affected any other ceph community infrastructure there evidence that build systems ceph github source repository were compromised new hosts ceph com download ceph com have been created sites have been rebuilt all content available download ceph com been verified all ceph com urls package locations now redirect there there still some content missing from download ceph com that will appear later today source tarballs will regenerated from git older release packages are being resigned with new release key download inktank com host been retired affected red hat customers have been notified further information available https securityblog redhat com 2015 09 17 users ceph packages should take action precautionary measure download newly-signed versions please see instructions below ceph community would like thank kai fabian initially alerting us this issue following steps should performed all nodes with ceph software installed replace apt keys debian ubuntu sudo apt-key del 17ed316d curl https git ceph com release asc sudo apt-key add - sudo apt-get update replace rpm keys fedora centos suse etc sudo rpm -e --allmatches title: v9.1.0 Infernalis release candidate released
author: sage
content: this first infernalis release candidate there have been some major changes since hammer upgrade process non-trivial please read carefully getting release candidate v9 1 0 packages are pushed ceph-deploy install --testing host known issues librbd librados abi compatibility broken careful installing this rc client machines e g those running qemu will fixed final v9 2 0 release major changes from hammer general ceph daemons are now managed via systemd with exception ubuntu trusty which still uses upstart ceph daemons run ceph user instead root red hat distros there also selinux policy rados rados cache tier can now proxy write operations base tier allowing writes handled without forcing migration object into cache shec erasure coding support longer flagged experimental shec trades some additional storage space faster repair there now unified queue thus prioritization client io recovery scrubbing snapshot trimming there have been many improvements low-level repair tooling ceph-objectstore-tool internal objectstore api been significantly cleaned order faciliate new storage backends like newstore rgw swift api now supports object expiration there are many swift api compatibility improvements rbd rbd du command shows actual usage quickly when object-map enabled object-map feature seen many stability improvements object-map exclusive-lock features can enabled disabled dynamically can now store user metadata set persistent librbd options associated with individual images new deep-flatten features allows flattening clone all its snapshots previously snapshots could flattened export-diff command command now faster uses aio there also new fast-diff feature –size argument can specified with suffix units e g --size 64g there new rbd status command that now shows who image open mapped cephfs can now rename snapshots there have been ongoing improvements around administration diagnostics check repair tools caching revocation client cache state due unused inodes been dramatically improved ceph-fuse client behaves better 32-bit hosts distro compatibility have decided drop support many older distributions that can move newer compiler toolchain e g hammer all distributions that support systemd centos 7 fedora debian jessie 8 x opensuse ceph daemons are now managed using native systemd files instead legacy sysvinit scripts example systemctl start dynamically assigned uid when user created your systems already have ceph user upgrading package will cause problems suggest first remove rename existing ceph user before upgrading when upgrading administrators have two options add following line ceph conf all hosts setuser match path var lib ceph type cluster- id this will make ceph daemons run root e drop privileges switch user ceph daemon data directory still owned by root newly deployed daemons will created with data owned by user ceph will run with reduced privileges upgraded daemons will continue run root fix data ownership during title: v9.2.0 Infernalis released
author: sage
content: this major release will foundation next stable series there have been some major changes since v0 94 x hammer upgrade process non-trivial please read these release notes carefully major changes from hammer general ceph daemons are now managed via systemd with exception ubuntu trusty which still uses upstart ceph daemons run ceph user instead root red hat distros there also selinux policy rados rados cache tier can now proxy write operations base tier allowing writes handled without forcing migration object into cache shec erasure coding support longer flagged experimental shec trades some additional storage space faster repair there now unified queue thus prioritization client io recovery scrubbing snapshot trimming there have been many improvements low-level repair tooling ceph-objectstore-tool internal objectstore api been significantly cleaned order faciliate new storage backends like newstore rgw swift api now supports object expiration there are many swift api compatibility improvements rbd rbd du command shows actual usage quickly when object-map enabled object-map feature seen many stability improvements object-map exclusive-lock features can enabled disabled dynamically can now store user metadata set persistent librbd options associated with individual images new deep-flatten features allows flattening clone all its snapshots previously snapshots could flattened export-diff command command now faster uses aio there also new fast-diff feature –size argument can specified with suffix units e g --size 64g there new rbd status command that now shows who image open mapped cephfs can now rename snapshots there have been ongoing improvements around administration diagnostics check repair tools caching revocation client cache state due unused inodes been dramatically improved ceph-fuse client behaves better 32-bit hosts distro compatibility have decided drop support many older distributions that can move newer compiler toolchain e g c 11 although still possible build ceph older distributions by installing backported development tools are building publishing release packages ceph com now build packages centos 7 later have dropped support centos 6 other rhel 6 derivatives like scientific linux 6 debian jessie 8 x later debian wheezy 7 x g incomplete support c 11 systemd ubuntu trusty 14 04 later ubuntu precise 12 04 longer supported fedora 22 later upgrading from firefly upgrading directly from firefly v0 80 z recommended possible direct upgrade without downtime recommend that clusters are first upgraded hammer v0 94 4 later v0 94 z release only then possible upgrade infernalis 9 2 z online upgrade see below offline upgrade directly from firefly all firefly osds must stopped marked down before any infernalis osds title: Melbourne Ceph Day - A recap with videos
author: timhildred
content: case didn t know ceph days are series regular events support ceph community that happen locations around world from new york berlin more recently apac shanghai melbourne melbourne edition november 5th 2015 australia first ever ceph day hosted clayton campus sponsor monash university about 60 uber ride from city centre monash also home part australia national research cloud nectar including ceph-backed storage capacity provided part research data services initiative watch this video get feel day about 2 minutes https www youtube com watch v vck6ksa0dn0 day sponsored by usual suspects fujitsu sandisk mellanox red hat monash provided excellent facilities that dwarfed number participants room 400 100 rsvped yes that pretty good somewhere between 50-70 turned that pretty normal attendees were mixed bunch ranging from complete neophytes looking see what fuss about sysadmins from medium sized companies experimenting with ceph pocs large academic institutions with massive production ceph clusters deployed speakers were heavily weighted towards vendor side which maybe expected community event relatively early uptake ceph australia that being said all presentations were focused providing value community rather than selling product patrick mcgarry ceph community director kicked with community state affairs his presentation included information about upcoming expanded ceph metrics platform what ceph user committee been mirror network new community infrastructure better contributor experience governance here https www youtube com watch v jocp3wbyv9e sandisk vekat kolli talked about contributions that he his team had been making improve ceph performance solid state drives ssds particular he shared how they d managed drastically improve ceph iops flash drives https www youtube com watch v f6vnxfo9x8y red hat brad hubbard provided tactical presentation how troubleshoot your ceph cluster including how properly diagnose your performance issues how tell your hang really hang massive toolbox can use your ceph cluster https www youtube com watch v yzx1onqrjmk suda from mellanox made clear that when reach certain scale can t solve your storage problems without good networking one key messages from his presentation that ceph will eat all bandwidth give perform better when have more https www youtube com watch v hngvk2bcln0 steve blair from monash laid out how needs researchers differ from those enterprise how they using ceph meet needs researchers from around australia why ceph especially useful when solving 4th paradigm problems https www youtube com watch v aznwqiedpfg tohohiko kimura from midokura had put together software-defined-everything poc using openstack ceph well his company neutron plugin software defined networking here how he did https www youtube com watch v 3cadzxdsbwa end day all presenters gathered stage speak together with audience they fielded questions everything from favourite deployment tools ceph-deploy versus ansible versus… erasure coding considerations what did yahoo state ceph front ends romana calamari what https www youtube com watch v bf5gs6kewli

title: v10.2.0 Jewel released
author: sage
content: this major release ceph will foundation next long-term stable release there have been many major changes since infernalis 9 2 x hammer 0 94 x releases upgrade process non-trivial please read these release notes carefully major changes from infernalis cephfs this first release which cephfs declared stable several features are disabled by default including snapshots multiple active mds servers repair disaster recovery tools are now feature-complete new cephfs-volume-manager module included that provides high-level interface creating shares openstack manila similar projects there now experimental support multiple cephfs file systems within single cluster rgw multisite feature been almost completely rearchitected rewritten support any number clusters sites bidirectional fail-over active active configurations can now access radosgw buckets via nfs experimental aws4 authentication protocol now supported there now support s3 request payer buckets new multitenancy infrastructure improves compatibility with swift which provides separate container namespace each user tenant openstack keystone v3 api now supported there are range other small swift api features compatibility improvements well including bulk delete slo static large objects rbd there new support mirroring asynchronous replication rbd images across clusters this implemented per-rbd image journal that can streamed across wan another site new rbd-mirror daemon that performs cross-cluster replication exclusive-lock object-map fast-diff journaling features can enabled disabled dynamically deep-flatten features can disabled dynamically -enabled rbd cli been rewritten provide command-specific help full bash completion support rbd snapshots can now renamed rados bluestore new osd backend included title: We've released the kraken!
author: TheAnalyst
content: this first release kraken series suitable use production deployments will maintained until next stable release next release luminous will completed spring 2017 get 11 2 0 quot kraken quot major changes from jewel rados new bluestore backend now stable disk format passing our failure stress testing although backend still flagged experimental encourage users try out non-production clusters non-critical data sets rados now experimental support overwrites erasure-coded pools because disk format implementation are yet finalized there special pool option that must enabled test new feature enabling this option cluster will permanently bar that cluster from being upgraded future versions now default asyncmessenger ms type async instead legacy simplemessenger most noticeable difference that now use fixed sized thread pool network connections instead two threads per socket with simplemessenger some osd failures are now detected almost immediately whereas previously author: TheAnalyst
content: this first development checkpoint release luminous series next long time release good start release luminous spring 17 major changes from kraken when assigning network public network cluster network network specification public network will used cluster network well older versions this would lead cluster services being bound 0 0 0 0 thus making cluster service even more publicly available than public services when only specifying cluster network will still result public services binding 0 0 0 0 some variants omap get keys omap get vals librados functions have been deprecated favor omap get vals2 omap get keys2 new methods include output argument indicating whether there are additional keys left fetch previously this had inferred from requested key count vs number keys returned this breaks with new osd-side limits number keys bytes that can returned by single omap request these limits were introduced by kraken are effectively disabled by default by setting very large limit 1 gb because users newly deprecated interface cannot tell whether they should fetch more keys case standalone calls c interface ioctx get omap keys vals librados been updated loop client side provide correct result via multiple calls osd case methods used building multi-operation transactions however client-side looping practical methods have been deprecated note that use either ioctx methods older librados versions deprecated methods any version librados will lead incomplete results when new osd limits are enabled previous versions client sent op wrong osd osd would reply with enxio rationale here that client osd clearly buggy want surface error clearly possible now only send enxio reply osd enxio on misdirected op option enabled by default this means that vm using librbd that previously would have gotten eio gone read-only will now see blocked hung io instead when configuring ceph-fuse mounts etc fstab new syntax available that uses quot ceph quot options column instead putting configuration device column old style syntax still works see documentation page quot mount cephfs your file systems table quot details notable changes bluestore avoid unnecessary copy with title: v12.1.0 Luminous RC released
author: TheAnalyst
content: this first release candidate luminous next long term stable release ceph luminous will foundation next long-term stable release series there have been major changes since kraken v11 2 z jewel v10 2 z major changes from kraken general ceph now simple built- web-based dashboard monitoring cluster status rados bluestore new bluestore backend ceph-osd now stable new default newly created osds bluestore manages data stored by each osd by directly managing physical hdds ssds without use intervening file system like xfs this provides greater performance features bluestore supports full data metadata checksums all data stored by ceph bluestore supports inline compression using zlib snappy lz4 ceph also supports zstd rgw compression zstd recommended bluestore performance reasons erasure coded pools now have full support overwrites allowing them used with rbd cephfs read more about ec overwrites ceph-mgr there new daemon ceph-mgr which required part any ceph deployment although io can continue when ceph-mgr down metrics will refresh some metrics-related calls e g ceph df may block recommend deploying several instances ceph-mgr reliability see notes upgrading below ceph-mgr daemon includes rest-based management api api still experimental somewhat limited will form basis api-based management ceph going forward overall scalability cluster improved have successfully tested clusters with 10 000 osds each osd can now have device class associated with e g hdd ssd allowing crush rules trivially map data subset devices system manually writing crush rules manual editing crush normally required can now optimize crush weights can now optimized maintain near-perfect distribution data across osds there also new upmap exception mechanism that allows individual pgs moved around achieve perfect distribution this requires luminous clients each osd now adjusts its default configuration based whether backing device hdd ssd manual tuning generally required prototype mclock qos queueing algorithm now available there now backoff mechanism that prevents osds from being overloaded by requests objects pgs that are currently able process io there simplified osd replacement process that more robust can query supported features apparent releases all connected daemons clients with ceph features can configure oldest ceph client version wish allow connect cluster via ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client ceph will prevent from enabling features that will break compatibility with those clients several sleep settings include osd recovery sleep osd snap trim sleep osd scrub sleep have been reimplemented work efficiently these are used some cases work around issues throttling background work rgw rgw metadata search backed by elasticsearch now supports end user requests service via rgw itself also supports custom metadata fields query language set restful apis were created users able search objects by their metadata new apis that allow control custom metadata fields were also added rgw now supports dynamic bucket index sharding number objects bucket grows rgw will automatically reshard bucket index response user intervention bucket size capacity planning required rgw introduces server side encryption uploaded objects with three options management encryption keys automatic encryption only recommended test setups customer provided keys similar amazon sse-c specification through use external key management service openstack barbician similar amazon sse-kms specification rgw now preliminary aws-like bucket policy api support now policy means express range new authorization concepts future will founation additional auth capabilities such sts group policy rgw consolidated several metadata index pools via use rados namespaces rbd rbd now full stable support erasure coded pools via new --data-pool option rbd create rbd mirroring rbd-mirror daemon now highly available recommend deploying several instances rbd-mirror reliability default rbd pool longer created automatically during cluster creation additionally name default pool used by rbd cli when pool specified can overridden via new rbd default pool configuration option initial support deferred image deletion via new rbd trash cli commands images even ones actively -use by clones can moved trash deleted later time new pool-level rbd mirror pool promote rbd mirror pool demote commands batch promote demote all mirrored images within pool mirroring now optionally supports configurable replication delay via rbd mirroring replay delay configuration option improved discard handling when object map feature enabled rbd cli import copy commands now detect sparse preserve sparse regions snapshots will now include creation timestamp cephfs multiple active mds daemons now considered stable number active mds servers may adjusted down active cephfs file system cephfs directory fragmentation now stable enabled by default new filesystems enable existing filesystems use quot ceph fs set allow dirfrags quot large very busy directories are sharded potentially distributed across multiple mds daemons automatically directory subtrees can explicitly pinned specific mds daemons cases where automatic load balancing desired effective miscellaneous release packages are now being built debian stretch distributions build now includes centos 7 x86 64 aarch64 debian 8 jessie x86 64 debian 9 stretch x86 64 ubuntu 16 04 xenial x86 64 aarch64 ubuntu 14 04 trusty x86 64 note that qa limited centos ubuntu xenial trusty cli changes ceph - ceph status command fresh look ceph osd mds mon versions summarizes versions running daemons ceph osd mds mon count-metadata similarly tabulates any other daemon metadata visible via ceph osd mds mon metadata commands ceph features summarizes features releases connected clients daemons ceph osd require-osd-release replaces old require release osds flags ceph osd pg-upmap ceph osd rm-pg-upmap ceph osd pg-upmap-items ceph osd new this should hidden from most users by user-facing tools like ceph-disk ceph osd destroy will mark osd destroyed remove its cephx lockbox keys however osd id crush map entry will remain place allowing id reused by replacement device with minimal data rebalancing ceph osd purge will remove all traces osd from cluster including its cephx encryption keys dm-crypt lockbox keys osd id crush map entry ceph osd ls-tree will output list osd ids under given crush name like host rack name this useful applying changes entire subtrees example ceph osd down ceph osd ls-tree rack1 ceph osd add rm - noout noin nodown noup allow noout nodown noin noup flags applied specific osds ceph log last n will output last n lines cluster log ceph mgr dump will dump mgrmap including currently active ceph-mgr daemon any standbys ceph osd crush swap-bucket will swap contents two crush buckets hierarchy while preserving buckets ids this allows entire subtree devices replaced e g replace entire host filestore osds with newly-imaged bluestore osds without disrupting distribution data across neighboring devices ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client configures oldest client release cluster required support title: v12.1.2 Luminous RC released
author: TheAnalyst
content: this third release candidate luminous next long term stable release ceph luminous v12 2 0 will foundation next long-term stable release series there have been major changes since kraken v11 2 z jewel v10 2 z upgrade process non-trivial please read these release notes carefully major changes from kraken general ceph now simple built- web-based dashboard monitoring cluster status rados bluestore new bluestore backend ceph-osd now stable new default newly created osds bluestore manages data stored by each osd by directly managing physical hdds ssds without use intervening file system like xfs this provides greater performance features bluestore supports full data metadata checksums all data stored by ceph bluestore supports inline compression using zlib snappy lz4 ceph also supports zstd rgw compression zstd recommended bluestore performance reasons fixme docs erasure coded pools now have full support overwrites allowing them used with rbd cephfs configuration option osd pool erasure code stripe width been replaced by osd pool erasure code stripe unit given ability overridden by erasure code profile setting stripe unit more details see erasure code profiles documentation rbd cephfs can use erasure coding with bluestore this may enabled by setting allow ec overwrites true pool since this relies bluestore checksumming deep scrubbing enabling this pool stored filestore allowed rados df json output now prints numeric values numbers instead strings mon osd max op age option been renamed mon osd warn op age default 32 seconds indicate generate warning this age there also new mon osd err op age ratio that expressed multitple mon osd warn op age default 128 roughly 60 minutes control when error generated default maximum size single rados object been reduced from 100gb 128mb 100gb limit completely impractical practice while 128mb limit bit high unreasonable have application written directly librados that using objects larger than 128mb may need adjust osd max object size semantics rados ls librados object listing operations have always been bit confusing that whiteout objects which logically don t exist will return enoent try access them are included results previously whiteouts only occurred cache tier pools luminous logically deleted snapshotted objects now result whiteout object result they will appear rados ls results even though trying read such object will result enoent rados listsnaps operation can used such case enumerate which snapshots are present this may seem bit strange less strange than having deleted- -snapshotted object appear all completely hidden from librados ability enumerate objects future versions ceph will likely include alternative object enumeration interface that makes more natural efficient enumerate all objects along with their snapshot clone metadata ceph-mgr there new daemon ceph-mgr which required part any ceph deployment although io can continue when ceph-mgr down metrics will refresh some metrics-related calls e g ceph df may block recommend deploying several instances ceph-mgr reliability see notes upgrading below ceph-mgr daemon includes rest-based management api api still experimental somewhat limited will form basis api-based management ceph going forward ceph-mgr also includes prometheus exporter plugin which can provide ceph perfcounters prometheus status ceph-mgr module enabled by default initially provides two commands ceph tell mgr osd status ceph tell mgr fs status these are high level colorized views complement existing cli overall scalability cluster improved have successfully tested clusters with 10 000 osds each osd can now have device class associated with e g hdd ssd allowing crush rules trivially map data subset devices system manually writing crush rules manual editing crush normally required can now optimize crush weights maintain near-perfect distribution data across osds fixme docs there also new upmap exception mechanism that allows individual pgs moved around achieve perfect distribution this requires luminous clients each osd now adjusts its default configuration based whether backing device hdd ssd manual tuning generally required prototype mclock qos queueing algorithm now available there now backoff mechanism that prevents osds from being overloaded by requests objects pgs that are currently able process io there simplified osd replacement process that more robust can query supported features apparent releases all connected daemons clients with ceph features can configure oldest ceph client version wish allow connect cluster via ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client ceph will prevent from enabling features that will break compatibility with those clients several sleep settings include osd recovery sleep osd snap trim sleep osd scrub sleep have been reimplemented work efficiently these are used some cases work around issues throttling background work deprecated crush ruleset property finally been removed please use crush rule instead osd pool get osd pool set commands osd pool default crush replicated ruleset option been removed replaced by osd pool default crush rule option by default -1 which means mon will pick first type replicated rule crush map replicated pools erasure coded pools have rules that are automatically created them they are specified pool creation time rgw rgw metadata search backed by elasticsearch now supports end user requests service via rgw itself also supports custom metadata fields query language set restful apis were created users able search objects by their metadata new apis that allow control custom metadata fields were also added rgw now supports dynamic bucket index sharding number objects bucket grows rgw will automatically reshard bucket index response user intervention bucket size capacity planning required rgw introduces server side encryption uploaded objects with three options management encryption keys automatic encryption only recommended test setups customer provided keys similar amazon sse-c specification through use external key management service openstack barbican similar amazon sse-kms specification rgw now preliminary aws-like bucket policy api support now policy means express range new authorization concepts future will foundation additional auth capabilities such sts group policy rgw consolidated several metadata index pools via use rados namespaces rbd rbd now full stable support erasure coded pools via new --data-pool option rbd create rbd mirroring rbd-mirror daemon now highly available recommend deploying several instances rbd-mirror reliability default rbd pool longer created automatically during cluster creation additionally name default pool used by rbd cli when pool specified can overridden via new rbd default pool configuration option initial support deferred image deletion via new rbd trash cli commands images even ones actively -use by clones can moved trash deleted later time new pool-level rbd mirror pool promote rbd mirror pool demote commands batch promote demote all mirrored images within pool mirroring now optionally supports configurable replication delay via rbd mirroring replay delay configuration option improved discard handling when object map feature enabled rbd cli import copy commands now detect sparse preserve sparse regions images snapshots will now include creation timestamp cephfs multiple active mds daemons now considered stable number active mds servers may adjusted down active cephfs file system cephfs directory fragmentation now stable enabled by default new filesystems enable existing filesystems use ceph fs set allow dirfrags large very busy directories are sharded potentially distributed across multiple mds daemons automatically directory subtrees can explicitly pinned specific mds daemons cases where automatic load balancing desired effective miscellaneous release packages are now being built debian stretch note that qa limited centos ubuntu xenial trusty distributions build now includes centos 7 x86 64 aarch64 debian 8 jessie x86 64 debian 9 stretch x86 64 ubuntu 16 04 xenial x86 64 aarch64 should hidden from most users by user-facing tools like ceph-disk ceph osd destroy will mark osd destroyed remove its cephx lockbox keys however osd id crush map entry will remain place allowing id
