standbys ceph mgr module ls will list active ceph-mgr modules ceph mgr module enable disable will enable disable named mgr module module must present configured mgr module path host where ceph-mgr running ceph osd crush swap-bucket will swap contents two crush buckets hierarchy while preserving buckets ids this allows entire subtree devices replaced e g replace entire host filestore osds with newly-imaged bluestore osds without disrupting distribution data across neighboring devices ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client configures oldest client release cluster required support other changes like crush tunables will fail with error they would violate this setting changing this setting also fails clients older than specified release are currently connected cluster ceph config-key dump dumps config-key entries their contents existing ceph config-key list only dumps key names values ceph config-key list deprecated favor ceph config-key ls ceph auth list deprecated favor ceph auth ls ceph osd crush rule list deprecated favor ceph osd crush rule ls ceph osd set- full nearfull backfillfull -ratio sets cluster-wide ratio various full thresholds when cluster refuses io when cluster warns about being close full when osd will defer rebalancing pg itself respectively ceph osd reweightn will specify reweight values multiple osds single command this equivalent series ceph osd reweight commands ceph osd crush class rm ls ls-osd manage new crush device class feature ceph crush set-device-class will set class particular devices note that specify non-existent class will created automatically ceph crush rm-device-class will instead remove class particular devices class contains more devices will automatically destoryed ceph osd crush rule create-replicated replaces old ceph osd crush rule create-simple command create crush rule replicated pool notably takes class argument device class rule should target e g ssd hdd ceph mon feature ls will list monitor features recorded monmap ceph mon feature set will set optional feature none these exist yet ceph tell help will now return usage summary major changes from jewel rados now default asyncmessenger ms type async instead legacy simplemessenger most noticeable difference that now use fixed sized thread pool network connections instead two threads per socket with simplemessenger some osd failures are now detected almost immediately whereas previously heartbeat timeout which defaults 20 seconds had expire this prevents io from blocking extended period failures where host remains ceph-osd process longer running size encoded osdmaps been reduced osds now quiesce scrubbing when recovery rebalancing progress rgw rgw now supports s3 multipart object copy-part api possible now reshard existing bucket offline offline bucket resharding currently requires that all io especially writes specific bucket quiesced automatic online resharding see new feature luminous above rgw now supports data compression objects civetweb version been upgraded 1 8 swift static website api now supported s3 support been added previously s3 bucket lifecycle api been added note that currently only supports object expiration support custom search filters been added ldap auth implementation support nfs version 3 been added rgw nfs gateway python binding been created librgw rbd rbd-mirror daemon now supports replicating dynamic image feature updates image metadata key value pairs from primary image non-primary image number image snapshots can optionally restricted configurable maximum rbd python api now supports asynchronous io operations cephfs libcephfs function definitions have been changed enable proper uid gid control library version been increased reflect interface change standby replay mds daemons now consume less memory workloads doing deletions scrub now repairs backtrace populates damage ls with discovered errors new pg files subcommand cephfs-data-scan can identify files affected by title: v12.1.3 Luminous (RC) released
author: TheAnalyst
content: this final release candidate luminous next long term stable release ceph luminous v12 2 0 will foundation next long-term stable release series there have been major changes since kraken v11 2 z jewel v10 2 z upgrade process non-trivial please read these release notes carefully major changes from kraken general ceph now simple built- web-based dashboard monitoring cluster status rados bluestore new bluestore backend ceph-osd now stable new default newly created osds bluestore manages data stored by each osd by directly managing physical hdds ssds without use intervening file system like xfs this provides greater performance features see storage devices bluestore config reference bluestore supports full data metadata checksums all data stored by ceph bluestore supports inline compression using zlib snappy lz4 ceph also supports zstd rgw compression zstd recommended bluestore performance reasons erasure coded pools now have full support overwrites allowing them used with rbd cephfs ceph-mgr there new daemon ceph-mgr which required part any ceph deployment although io can continue when ceph-mgr down metrics will refresh some metrics-related calls e g ceph df may block recommend deploying several instances ceph-mgr reliability see notes upgrading below ceph-mgr daemon includes rest-based management api api still experimental somewhat limited will form basis api-based management ceph going forward ceph-mgr also includes prometheus exporter plugin which can provide ceph perfcounters prometheus ceph-mgr now zabbix plugin using zabbix sender sends trapper events zabbix server containing high-level information ceph cluster this makes easy monitor ceph cluster status send out notifications case malfunction overall scalability cluster improved have successfully tested clusters with 10 000 osds each osd can now have device class associated with e g hdd ssd allowing crush rules trivially map data subset devices system manually writing crush rules manual editing crush normally required there also new upmap exception mechanism that allows individual pgs moved around achieve perfect distribution this requires luminous clients each osd now adjusts its default configuration based whether backing device hdd ssd manual tuning generally required prototype mclock qos queueing algorithm now available there now backoff mechanism that prevents osds from being overloaded by requests objects pgs that are currently able process io there simplified osd replacement process that more robust can query supported features apparent releases all connected daemons clients with ceph features can configure oldest ceph client version wish allow connect cluster via ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client ceph will prevent from enabling features that will break compatibility with those clients several sleep settings include osd recovery sleep osd snap trim sleep osd scrub sleep have been reimplemented work efficiently these are used some cases work around issues throttling background work crush choose args encoding been changed make architecture-independent pools are now expected associated with application using them upon completing upgrade luminous cluster will attempt associate existing pools known applications e cephfs rbd rgw -use pools that are associated application will generate health warning any unassociated pools can manually associated using new ceph osd pool application enable command more details see associate pool application documentation added new commands pg force-recovery pg-force-backfill use them boost recovery backfill priority specified pgs they recovered backfilled before any other note that these commands don t interrupt ongoing recovery backfill merely queue specified pgs before others they recovered backfilled soon possible new commands pg cancel-force-recovery pg cancel-force-backfill restore default recovery backfill priority previously forced pgs ceph-mon added new configuration public bind addr support dynamic environments like kubernetes when set ceph mon daemon could bind locally ip address advertise different ip address public addr network rgw rgw metadata search backed by elasticsearch now supports end user requests service via rgw itself also supports custom metadata fields query language set restful apis were created users able search objects by their metadata new apis that allow control custom metadata fields were also added rgw now supports dynamic bucket index sharding number objects bucket grows rgw will automatically reshard bucket index response user intervention bucket size capacity planning required this feature needs enabled by setting rgw dynamic resharding true ceph conf rgw introduces server side encryption uploaded objects with three options management encryption keys automatic encryption only recommended test setups customer provided keys similar amazon sse-c specification through use external key management service openstack barbican similar amazon sse-kms specification encryption rgw now preliminary aws-like bucket policy api support now policy means express range new authorization concepts future will foundation additional auth capabilities such sts group policy bucket policies rgw consolidated several metadata index pools via use rados namespaces pools s3 object tagging api been added while apis are supported get put delete object tags put object api there support tags policies amp lifecycle yet rgw multisite now supports enabling disabling sync bucket level rbd rbd now full stable support erasure coded pools via new --data-pool option rbd create rbd mirroring rbd-mirror daemon now highly available recommend deploying several instances rbd-mirror reliability rbd mirroring rbd-mirror daemon should utilize unique ceph user ids per instance support new mirroring dashboard default rbd pool longer created automatically during cluster creation additionally name default pool used by rbd cli when pool specified can overridden via new rbd default pool configuration option initial support deferred image deletion via new rbd trash cli commands images even ones actively -use by clones can moved trash deleted later time new pool-level rbd mirror pool promote rbd mirror pool demote commands batch promote demote all mirrored images within pool mirroring now optionally supports configurable replication delay via rbd mirroring replay delay configuration option improved discard handling when object map feature enabled rbd cli import copy commands now detect sparse preserve sparse regions images snapshots will now include creation timestamp specifying user authorization capabilities rbd clients been simplified general syntax using rbd capability profiles mon profile rbd osd profile rbd -read-only pool pool-name more details see user management documentation cephfs multiple active mds daemons now considered stable number active mds servers may adjusted down active cephfs file system cephfs directory fragmentation now stable enabled by default new filesystems enable existing filesystems use ceph fs set allow dirfrags large very busy directories are sharded potentially distributed across multiple mds daemons automatically directory subtrees can explicitly pinned specific mds daemons cases where automatic load balancing desired effective client keys can now created using new ceph fs authorize command create keys with access given cephfs file system all its data pools apply mode cephfs-journal-tool been removed when running df cephfs filesystem comprising exactly one data pool result now reflects file storage space used available that data pool fuse client only miscellaneous release packages are now being built debian stretch note that qa limited centos ubuntu xenial trusty distributions build now includes centos 7 x86 64 aarch64 debian 8 jessie x86 64 debian 9 stretch x86 64 ubuntu 16 04 xenial x86 64 aarch64 ubuntu 14 04 trusty x86 64 first release ceph freebsd available which contains full set features other than bluestore will run everything needed build storage cluster clients all access methods are available albeit cephfs only accessible through fuse implementation rbd images can mounted freebsd systems through rbd-ggate ceph versions are released through regular freebsd ports packages system most current version available net ceph-devel once luminous goes into official release this version will available net ceph future development releases will available via net ceph-devel more details about this port are readme freebsd cli changes ceph - ceph status command fresh look ceph mgr metadata will dump metadata associated with each mgr daemon ceph versions ceph osd mds mon mgr versions summarize versions running daemons ceph osd mds mon mgr count-metadata similarly tabulates any other daemon metadata visible via ceph osd mds mon mgr metadata commands ceph features summarizes features releases connected clients daemons ceph osd require-osd-release replaces old require release osds flags ceph osd pg-upmap ceph osd rm-pg-upmap ceph osd pg-upmap-items ceph osd rm-pg-upmap-items can explicitly manage upmap items see using pg-upmap ceph osd getcrushmap returns crush map version number stderr ceph osd setcrushmap version will only inject updated crush map version matches this allows crush maps updated offline then reinjected into cluster without fear clobbering racing changes e g by newly added osds changes by other administrators ceph osd create been replaced by ceph osd new this should hidden from most users by user-facing tools like ceph-disk ceph osd destroy will mark osd destroyed remove its cephx lockbox keys however osd id crush map entry will remain place allowing id reused by replacement device with minimal data rebalancing ceph osd purge will remove all traces osd from cluster including its cephx encryption keys dm-crypt lockbox keys osd id crush map entry ceph osd ls-tree will output list osd ids under given crush name like host rack name this useful applying changes entire subtrees example ceph osd down ceph osd ls-tree rack1 ceph osd add rm - noout noin nodown noup allow noout noin nodown noup flags applied specific osds ceph log last n will output last n lines cluster log ceph mgr dump will dump mgrmap including currently active ceph-mgr daemon any standbys ceph mgr module ls will list active ceph-mgr modules ceph mgr module enable disable will enable disable named mgr module module must present configured mgr module path host where ceph-mgr running ceph osd crush swap-bucket will swap contents two crush buckets hierarchy while preserving buckets ids this allows entire subtree devices replaced e g replace entire host filestore osds with newly-imaged bluestore osds without disrupting distribution data across neighboring devices ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client configures oldest client release cluster required support other changes like crush tunables will fail with error they would violate this setting changing this setting also fails clients older than specified release are currently connected cluster ceph config-key dump dumps config-key entries their contents existing ceph config-key list only dumps key names values ceph config-key list deprecated favor ceph config-key ls ceph config-key put deprecated favor title: New in Luminous: BlueStore
author: sage
content: mbluestore new storage backend ceph boasts better performance roughly 2x writes full data checksumming built- compression new default storage backend ceph osds luminous v12 2 z will used by default when provisioning new osds with ceph-disk ceph-deploy ceph-ansible how fast roughly speaking bluestore about twice fast filestore performance more consistent with lower tail latency reality course much more complicated than that large writes avoid double-write that filestore did can twice fast except that many filestore deployments put journal separate ssd that benefit may masked small random writes significantly better even when compared filestore with journal except less clear when using nvme which tends bottlenecked actual storage device cpu testing ongoing key value data though significantly better avoiding some very ugly behavior that can crop filestore some rgw workloads example saw write performance improve by 3x avoid throughput collapse seen filestore due quot splitting quot when filling cluster with data small sequential reads using raw librados are slower bluestore this only appears affect microbenchmarks this somewhat deliberate bluestore doesn t implement its own readahead since everything sitting top rados its own readahead sequential reads using those higher-level interfaces like rbd cephfs are generally great unlike filestore bluestore copy- -write performance with rbd volumes cephfs files that were recently snapshotted will much better expect another blog post next few weeks with some real data deeper dive into bluestore performance that said bluestore still work progress continue identify issues make improvements this first stable release important milestone by means end our journey--only end beginning square peg round hole ceph osds perform two main functions replicating data across network other osds along with rebalancing healing everything else that comes with that storing data locally attached device hard disk ssd some combination two second local storage piece currently handled by existing filestore module which stores objects files xfs file system there quite bit history how ended with precise architecture interfaces that did central challenge that osd built around transactional updates those are awkward inefficient implement properly top standard file system end found there nothing wrong with xfs simply wrong tool job looking filestore design today find that most its shortcomings are related hackery required adapt our interface posix problems with ceph xfs isolation how does bluestore work bluestore clean implementation our internal objectstore interface from first principles motivated specifically by workloads expect bluestore built top raw underlying block device block devices embeds rocksdb key value database managing its internal metadata small internal adapter component called bluefs implements file-system-like interface that provides just enough functionality allow rocksdb store its files share same raw device with bluestore biggest difference notice between older filestore-based osds e g any osds deployed with ceph prior luminous bluestore ones what partitions mount point look like filestore osd see something like lsblk … sdb 8 16 0 931 5g 0 disk ├─sdb1 8 17 0 930 5g 0 part var lib ceph osd ceph-56 └─sdb2 8 18 0 1023m 0 part … df -h … dev sdb1 931g 487g 444g 53 var lib ceph osd ceph-56 ls -al var lib ceph osd ceph-56 … drwxr-xr-x 180 root root 16384 aug 30 21 55 current lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 58 jun 4 2015 journal - gt dev disk by-partuuid 538da076-0136-4c78-9af4-79bb40d7cbbd … that there small journal partition although often this separate ssd journal symlink data directory pointing separate journal paritition current directory that contains all actual object files df command shows how much device used since bluestore consumes raw block devices things are bit different lsblk … sdf 8 80 0 3 7t 0 disk ├─sdf1 8 81 0 100m 0 part var lib ceph osd ceph-75 └─sdf2 8 82 0 3 7t 0 part … df -h … dev sdf1 97m 5 4m 92m 6 var lib ceph osd ceph-75 … ls -al var lib ceph osd ceph-75 … lrwxrwxrwx 1 ceph ceph 58 aug 8 18 33 block - gt dev disk by-partuuid 80d28eb7-a7e7-4931-866d-303693f1efc4 … notice there data directory now tiny 100mb partition with just handful files rest device looks like large unused partition with block symlink data directory pointing this where bluestore putting all its data performing io directly raw device using linux asynchronous libaio infrastructure from ceph-osd process can still see per-osd utilization via standard ceph osd df command that what after can longer see underlying object files like used there new trick looking behind curtain see what each osd storing that works both bluestore filestore based osds osd stopped can mount osd data via fuse with mkdir mnt foo ceph-objectstore-tool --op fuse --data-path var lib ceph osd ceph-75 --mountpoint mnt foo also possible mount online osd assuming fuse configured correctly by enabling osd objectstore fuse config option fuse directory will appear osd data directory this generally recommended just recommended that users make any changes files filestore-based osd directory multiple devices bluestore can run against combination slow fast devices similar filestore except that bluestore generally able make much better use fast device filestore journal device often placed faster ssd only used writes bluestore internal journaling needed consistency much lighter-weight usually behaving like metadata journal only journaling small writes when faster necessary rest fast device can used store retrieve internal metadata bluestore can manage three devices required main device block symlink stores object data usually metadata too optional db device block db symlink stores much metadata rocksdb will fit whatever doesn t fit will spill back onto main device optional wal device block wal symlink stores just internal journal rocksdb write-ahead log general recommendation take much ssd space have available osd use block db device when using ceph-disk this accomplished with --block db argument ceph-disk prepare dev sdb --block db dev sdc by default partition will created sdc device that 1 main device size this can overridden with bluestore block db size config option more exotic possibility would use three devices primary hdd main device part ssd db device smaller nvdimm-backed device wal note that can expect some changes here add bluestore support new ceph-volume tool that will eventually replace ceph-disk expect backport all new ceph-volume functionality luminous when ready more information see bluestore configuration guide memory usage one nice thing about filestore that used normal linux file system which meant kernel responsible managing memory caching data metadata particular kernel can use all available ram cache then release soon memory needed something else because bluestore implemented userspace part osd manage our own cache have fewer memory management tools our disposal bottom line that with bluestore there bluestore cache size configuration option that controls how much memory each osd will use bluestore cache by default this 1 gb hdd-backed osds 3 gb ssd-backed osds can set whatever appropriate your environment see bluestore configuration guide more information one caveat that memory accounting currently imperfect allocator tcmalloc our case incurs some overhead allocations heap can become fragmented over time fragmentation prevents some freed memory from being released back operating system result there usually some disparity between what bluestore osd thinks using actual memory consumed by process rss order 1 5x can see this disparity yourself by comparing ceph-osd title: New in Luminous: Erasure Coding for RBD and CephFS
author: sage
content: luminous now fully supports overwrites erasure coded ec rados pools allowing rbd cephfs well rgw directly consume erasure coded pools this potential dramatically reduce overall cost per terabyte ceph systems since usual 3x storage overhead replication can reduced more like 1 2x 2x depending choice erasure code background ceph rados object store originally built around replication--usually 2x 3x this comparatively simple implement although still surprisingly difficult get right cp distributed system served us well some time with firefly release may 2014 added support erasure coded ec pools erasure codes allow ceph stripe object data over k osds while adding m additional chunks with encoded redundancy information this works like parity traditional raid system erasure codes typically generalize almost any value k m whereas raid5 fixes m 1 raid6 fixes m 2 ceph erasure codes are implemented via plugins that include conventional reed-soloman libraries with optimizations intel arm architectures local reconstruction code lrc plugin shec shingled erasure code however until now ec pools only allowed object appends deletions--overwrites were supported this allowed ec pools used rgw object storage cold tier behind replicated cache tier rbd cephfs could use ec pools directly given that erasure coding significantly reduces overall cost per gigabyte system this less than satisfying many users consistency after failure reason this limitation difficulty maintaining consistency something that ceph always been very particular about there failure while updating object that replicated recovery straightforward regardless how many which replicas ended with new old version object example above three replicas object initially contain content quot quot then update overwriting with quot b quot interrupted by failure such that only two three replicas are updated can either roll third replica forward b roll first two replicas back either choice would make system consistent rados because replica isn t acknowledged until all replicas are updated either option would fine currently roll forward case erasure coded object things are bit more complicated instead three identical complete copies object content spread over above example four objects each with 1 4th data two erasure objects p q there failure mid-update only three quot quot objects are updated with new quot b quot content have problem 4 2 erasure code requires any 4 shards reconstruct original content have only three new three old such that neither can reconstructed this basic problem generalized version -called quot raid hole quot many systems even ones used widely production sweep this problem under rug most time they get away with usually because whoever submitted title: v13.1.0 Mimic RC1 released
author: TheAnalyst
content: this first release candidate mimic next long term release while this final production release yet consider testing this your testing non production clusters preview upcoming features importantly report any bugs tracker notable changes core pg force-recovery command will work erasure-coded pgs when luminous monitor running along with mimic osd please use recommended upgrade order monitors before osds avoid this issue sample crush-location-hook script been removed its output equivalent built- default behavior been replaced with example crush documentation -f option rados tool now means –format instead –force consistency with ceph tool format config diff output via admin socket changed now reflects source each config option e g default config file command line well final active value commands variously marked del delete remove etc should now all normalized rm commands already supporting alternatives rm remain backward-compatible this changeset applies radosgw-admin cli well monitors will now prune -disk full maps number maps grows above certain number mon osdmap full prune min default 10000 thus preventing unbounded growth monitor data store this feature enabled by default can disabled by setting mon osdmap full prune enabled false rados list-inconsistent-obj format changes various error strings have been improved example oi oi attr errors which stands object info now info e g oi attr missing now info missing object selected object info now json format instead string attribute errors attr value mismatch attr name mismatch only apply user attributes only user attributes are output have internal leading underscore stripped there are hash information errors hinfo missing hinfo corrupted hinfo inconsistency then hashinfo added with json format information information corrupt then hashinfo string containing value there are snapset errors snapset missing snapset corrupted snapset inconsistency then snapset added with json format information information corrupt then snapset string containing value there are object information errors info missing info corrupted obj size info mismatch object info inconsistency then object info added with json format information instead string information corrupt then object info string containing value rados list-inconsistent-snapset format changes various error strings have been improved example ss attr errors which stands snapset info now snapset e g ss attr missing now snapset missing error snapset mismatch been renamed snapset error better reflect what means head snapset information output json format snapset this means that even when there are head errors head object will output when any shard error this head object there show snapset that used determining errors osd mon report interval min option been renamed osd mon report interval osd mon report interval max unused been eliminated this value been customized your cluster then your configuration should adjusted order avoid reverting default value config-key interface can store arbitrary binary blobs json can only express printable strings binary blobs are present ceph config-key dump command will show them something like gt gt bootstrap auth keys will now generated automatically fresh deployment these keys will also generated missing during upgrade osd force-create-pg command now requires force option proceed because command dangerous declares that data loss permanent instructs cluster proceed with empty pg its place without making any further efforts find missing data cephfs upgrading mds cluster 12 2 3 will result all active mds exiting due feature incompatibilities once upgraded mds comes online even standby operators may ignore error messages continue upgrading restarting follow this upgrade sequence reduce number ranks 1 ceph fs set max mds 1 deactivate all other ranks ceph mds deactivate shutdown standbys leaving one active mds upgrade single active mds then upgrade start standbys finally restore previous max mds see also https tracker ceph com issues 23172 several ceph mds commands have been obsoleted replaced by equivalent ceph fs commands - mds dump - gt fs dump - mds getmap - gt fs dump - mds stop - gt mds deactivate - mds set max mds - gt fs set max mds - mds set - gt fs set - mds cluster down - gt fs set cluster down true - mds cluster up - gt fs set cluster down false - mds add data pool - gt fs add data pool - mds remove data pool - gt fs rm data pool - mds rm data pool - gt fs rm data pool new cephfs file system attributes session timeout session autoclose are configurable via ceph fs set mds config options mds session timeout mds session autoclose mds max file size are now obsolete multiple mds feature now standard now enabled by default ceph fs set allow multimds now deprecated will removed future release directory fragmentation feature now standard now enabled by default ceph fs set allow dirfrags now deprecated will removed future release mds daemons now activate deactivate based value max mds accordingly ceph mds deactivate been deprecated now redundant taking cephfs cluster down now done by setting down flag which deactivates all mds example ceph fs set cephfs down true preventing standbys from joining new actives formerly now deprecated cluster down flag file system now accomplished by setting joinable flag this useful mostly testing that file system may quickly brought down deleted new cephfs file system attributes session timeout session autoclose are configurable via ceph fs set mds config options mds session timeout mds session autoclose mds max file size are now obsolete each mds rank now maintains table that tracks open files their ancestor directories recovering mds can quickly get open files pathes significantly reducing time loading inodes open files mds creates table automatically does exist cephfs snapshot now stable enabled by default new filesystems enable snapshot existing filesystems use command ceph fs set allow new snaps -disk format snapshot metadata changed old format metadata can properly handled multiple active mds configuration guarantee all snapshot metadata existing filesystems get updated perform sequence upgrading mds cluster strictly see http docs ceph com docs master cephfs upgrading filesystems that have ever enabled snapshot multiple-active mds feature disabled by new version mon this will cause restore previous max mds step above url fail -enable feature either delete all old snapshots scrub whole filesystem ceph daemon scrub path force recursive repair ceph daemon scrub path mdsdir force recursive repair rbd rbd c api rbd discard method now enforces maximum length 2gb match c api image discard method this restriction prevents overflow result code rbd cli lock list json xml output changed rbd cli showmapped json xml output changed rbd now optionally supports simplified image clone semantics where non-protected snapshots can cloned snapshots with linked clones can removed space automatically reclaimed once all remaining linked clones are detached this feature enabled by default osd require-min-compat-client flag set mimic later can overridden via rbd default clone format configuration option rbd now supports deep copy images rgw rgw beast frontend now declared stable ready production use http frontends details civetweb frontend been updated latest 1 10 release s3 api now support multi factor authentication refer rgw support multifactor authentication details rgw now sync plugin sync aws clouds with s3 like apis mgr read-only ceph manager dashboard introduced ceph luminous been replaced with new implementation providing drop- replacement offering number additional management features access new dashboard first content: this first stable release mimic next long term release series please read upgrade notes from previous releases carefully before upgrading major changes from luminous dashboard read-only ceph manager dashboard introduced ceph luminous been replaced with new implementation inspired by derived from openattic ceph management tool providing drop- replacement offering number additional management features rados config options can now centrally stored managed by monitor monitor daemon uses significantly less disk space when undergoing recovery rebalancing operations async recovery feature reduces tail latency requests when osds are recovering from recent failure osd preemption scrub by conflicting requests reduces tail latency rgw rgw can now replicate zone subset buckets external cloud storage service like s3 rgw now supports s3 multi-factor authentication api versioned buckets beast frontend long expermiental considered stable ready use cephfs snapshots are now stable when combined with multiple mds daemons rbd image clones longer require explicit protect unprotect steps images can deep-copied including any clone linkage parent image associated snapshots new pools with altered data layouts upgrading from luminous notes recommend avoid creating any rados pools while upgrade process can monitor progress your upgrade each stage with ceph versions command title: Rook: Automating Ceph for Kubernetes
author: tnielsen
content: rook orchestrator storage services that run kubernetes cluster rook v0 8 release are excited say that orchestration around ceph stabilized point declared beta haven t yet started ceph cluster with rook now time take spin may wondering what rook why should care ceph been running production clusters years why big deal now have managed ceph cluster before know many intricacies required setup maintain storage cluster rook will now simplify automate many those difficulties taking advantage kubernetes distributed platform rook implemented with operator which means administrator only have worry about declaring quot desired state quot cluster rook operator will watch your declared settings then apply configuration cluster state that will managed by operator includes everything necessary get cluster running keep healthy this post will touch some details what rook will manage mons first element any ceph cluster quorum monitors mons typically there are three mons running cluster they must remain highly available maintain their quorum else data cluster will available when create cluster rook will start mons unique nodes ensure they are quorum monitor mons periodically every minute ensure they remain quorum mon goes down does automatically restart with built- kubernetes mechanisms operator will add new mon quorum remove failed mon from quorum update clients ceph daemons with ip addresses mons when they failover mgr mgr stateless service that must remain running provide metrics other features cluster beyond starting mgr its core responsibilities rook configures two mgr plugins collect prometheus metrics prometheus running cluster run ceph dashboard including service endpoint connect osds most challenging part cluster typically osds core storage components cluster large clusters have many them manually setting them monitoring them last thing want rook will configure them one two modes depending how much control want keep over individual devices see this topic more details settings available osds fully automated simplest way rook initialize osds by declaring that want quot use all nodes quot quot use all devices quot this means that operator will automatically start osds all nodes kubernetes cluster that have available devices available devices are discovered by rook initialized with osds with simple criteria device partitions device formatted file systems rook will never attempt consume device that does satisfy that criteria when operator completed typically within minutes will have storage cluster with all osds configured fully declarative second mode configure your osds gives much more control over which nodes which devices consume cluster there are number settings with varying levels automated control nodes declare specific list nodes where osds should started use kubernetes placement constructs declare set nodes based labels devices declare individual device names which start osds declare more general filter device names which start osds specify high performance ssd nvme device which create metadata partitions bluestore with bluestore data partition different device this mode gives full control over which devices will consumed while taking care all details initializing osds client access kubernetes clients who need storage will use persistent volume attached mounted pod rook provides flexvolume plugin that will make easy your pods consume storage from ceph cluster all need declare storage class with pool consume then declare pvc your pod that points storage class this example will explain all details mounting rbd image your pod rgw beyond basic rados cluster rook will also help manage your object store when declare that want object store your cluster rook will create metadata data pools object store start rgw daemon running with multiple instances higher reliability desired create kubernetes service provide load balancing across rgw daemons voila object storage available your cluster mds last least rook will configure cephfs scenarios where need shared file system cluster when declare that want file system your cluster rook will create metadata data pools cephfs create file system start mds with desired number active standby instances file system can now consumed by pods cluster either by sharing same path independent path cephfs each pod see this example declaring kubernetes volume with rook volume plugin ceph tools even with all automation know will still need access full ceph tools run some maintenance tasks over time more automation added should need these tools less less meantime need run ceph tools all need start toolbox else connect existing daemon container such mon execute tools what next all rook requires run kubernetes cluster where storage configured rook goal make your life easier configure storage far are just scratching surface what can automated simplified with management ceph are actively developing rook project are planning number features coming soon hope join community look forward hearing from have any questions feedback come find us rook slack talk soon

content: this summer lucky get selected internship cern cern openlab summer student worked storage group nine weeks summer project evaluating ceph deployments with rook previously had amazing reduced cern currently uses combination kickstart puppet configure manage ceph deployments which poses some time constraints with recent rook ceph integration being beta stage made sense evaluate see author: sage
content: ceph storage clusters ultimately rely physical hardware devices--hdds ssds--that can fail starting nautilus management tracking physical devices now handled by ceph furthermore added infrastructure collect device health metrics e g smart predict device failures before they happen either via built- pre-trained prediction model via saas service managing devices ceph always taken approach that storage devices are just one many physical components that can fail instead focused attention failure storage daemons themselves whether bad cpu network link memory power supply storage device that failed end result storage daemon process stops system must cope this generally worked out well except that when fault does occur often tedious trace failure daemon say osd 123 back failing device what device name last held which hosts although multi-path devices were tested ceph should report all hosts where device been consumed health metrics nautilus can also monitor health metrics these devices sata devices this done via smart sas nvme devices there are similar standards that are mostly collectively referred smart by humans despite smart technically being sata standard content each scrape comes from smartctl command version 7 0 smartmontools required this work just released dec 30 2018 that version adds json output mode that our scraper consumes this version made its way title: Part - 1 : BlueStore (Default vs. Tuned) Performance Comparison
author: karan
content: acknowledgments would like thank bbva cisco intel providing cutting edge hardware used run red hat ceph storage 3 2 all-flash performance poc tests results provided this blog series joint effort partnership formed by bbva intel cisco red hat all partners have worked together produce performance baseline software defined storage building block based red hat ceph storage with cisco intel hardware technology executive summary tuning ceph configuration all-flash cluster resulted material performance improvements compared default out- - -box configuration such delivering 134 higher iops 70 lower average latency 90 lower tail latency all-flash cluster rhcs all-flash introduction all-flash storage systems offer several benefits businesses this includes high performance terms both high throughput lower latencies low tco with reduced power cooling consumption over traditional hard drive based storage systems global digital transformation requires modernization enterprise infrastructure improve performance responsiveness resiliency almost all critical business applications with proliferation complex application stacks databases new breed workloads storage data have become nervous system today businesses only way achieve storage nirvana use software-defined scale-out storage technology which built exascale red hat ceph storage rhcs open source massively scalable software-defined storage that all resilience durability reliability needed enterprise storage workloads with advancement nand technology flash media storage are becoming more affordable rhcs takes center stage being able deliver millions iops low latency catering customers most demanding storage intensive workload needs high performance latency sensitive workloads often consume storage via block device interface ceph delivers block storage clients with help rbd librbd library which thin layer that sits top rados figure-1 taking advantage all features rados offer rbd block devices are highly distributed nature stripes block device image over multiple objects red hat ceph storage cluster where each object gets mapped placement group distributed placement groups are spread across separate ceph osds throughout cluster this greatly enhances parallelism when accessing data from rbd volume figure 1 rhcs architecture components rhcs block devices are thin-provisioned resizable store data striped over multiple osds ceph cluster rhcs block devices leverage rados capabilities such self healing replication consistency ceph opensource project with thriving community over last few releases there been significant effort performance optimization all-flash clusters some these enhancements are introduction bluestore new storage backed osd starting rhcs 3 2 bluestore feature ga bluestore provides massive performance gains over old filestore backend by simplifying io datapath avoiding double write penalties reducing cpu usage together with bluestore numerous other performance improvements core ceph helped reduce osd cpu consumption especially flash media osds bluestore introduction bluestore new backend object store ceph osd daemons original object store filestore requires file system top raw block devices objects are then written file system unlike original filestore back end bluestore stores object directly block devices without any file system interface which improves performance cluster learn more about bluestore follow red hat ceph documentation bluestore under covers figure-2 shows how bluestore interacts with block device data directly written raw block device all metadata operations are managed by rocksdb device containing osd divided between rocksdb metadata actual user data stored cluster user data objects are stored blobs directly raw block device once data been written block device rocksdb metadata gets updated with required details about new data blobs rocksdb embedded high-performance key-value store that excels with flash-storage rocksdb can t directly write raw disk device needs underlying filesystem store persistent data this where bluefs comes bluefs filesystem developed with minimal feature set needed by rocksdb store its sst files rocksdb uses wal transaction log persistent storage unlike filestore where all writes went first journal bluestore have two different datapaths writes one were data written directly block device other were use deferred writes with deferred writes data gets written wal device later asynchronously flushed disk bluestore number possible storage layout configurations main device that stores object data optional rocksdb device that stores metadata optional wal device that stores transaction logs example our test environment configured main device intel p4500 drive this where user data will stored then configured wal rocksdb devices faster intel optane p4800 drive having wal rocksdb high performing drive will give us more iops with lower latency new feature bluestore that enables compression data lowest level compression enabled data blobs allocated raw device will compressed this means that any data written into rh ceph storage matter client used rbd rados etc can benefit from this feature additional benefit bluestore that stores data meta-data cluster with checksums increased integrity whenever data read from persistent storage its checksum verified figure 2 author: tnielsen
content: are excited announce number significant features improvements ceph operator kubernetes rook v1 1 major themes csi driver ready production dynamic bucket provisioning object storage connections external ceph cluster configuration mons osds top dynamic underlying storage enablement ceph manager modules from cluster cr upgrade maintenance improvements osd configuration improvements placement improvements csi driver csi driver ready prime time now can take full advantage dynamic provisioning with ceph-csi driver including dynamic provisioning rbd rwo access dynamic provisioning cephfs rwx access rook now enables csi driver by default both new upgraded clusters encourage create new storage class pointing csi provisioner create all new volumes based csi snapshots rbd volumes are also available snapshot api defined by csi interface still alpha state will need enable feature gate test out this feature full list csi features their status see ceph-csi github repo csi driver vs flex driver flexvolume driver taking back seat csi driver all future development being focused csi driver while flex driver still fully supported invite start this transition now after upgrade from v1 0 flex driver will continue run ensure your volumes keep running some point future flexvolume driver will deprecated will ensure your volumes have smooth path forward one reason would still need use flex driver are running k8s 1 12 earlier csi interface only declared stable starting k8s 1 13 therefore cannot support csi driver older versions kubernetes are still using flex driver new feature take advantage this release ability resize volumes yes heard right can now resize volumes bucket provisioning have ever wondered why object storage wasn t available pvc object storage always been treated differently by kubernetes now have solved this challenge brought this pattern dynamic provisioning buckets your ceph object store when admin wants expose object storage their cluster they start by defining storage class that points ceph cluster where object storage configured with rgw buckets can then provisioned by users when they request object bucket claim this follows standard kubernetes pattern pvcs except now available object storage well get started see section titled quot object storage buckets quot ceph examples page external ceph cluster already have ceph cluster running want your k8s applications consume that storage now possible with rook when this mode enabled rook will manage external cluster will simply consume order connect only need three pieces information external cluster ceph fsid external cluster monitor ip addresses external cluster-admin key once cephcluster created with this connection information rook will immediately connect that cluster this feature assumes that network connectivity been established between external ceph cluster local kubernetes environment achieve this use host networking makes that connection simple other options are also possible such having your external cluster same subnet your service pool ips customizing your ip routing one more thing rook can still bootstrap other crds kubernetes such object filesystem nfs this case these resources will run managed by rook local kubernetes even while persistence all external ceph cluster clients cluster won t even recognize that storage running elsewhere all connection information through csi driver rgw endpoint other services will storage available local cluster try out today by following walkthrough setting connection external cluster let us know how goes dynamic underlying storage ceph monitors osds require place persist your data monitors need access directory store their database until now this only achieved rook by bind mounting directory from host machine into container now rook runs cloud provider can take advantage kubernetes persistent storage support attach persistent volume claim pvc with filesystem ceph monitor store will then live pv just like other standard k8s storage ceph object storage daemons osds require raw block devices their implementation attaching storage with pvcs similar monitors difference that pvc must presented raw block device filesystem this new feature brings lot more flexibility run ceph cloud provider even your -premise clusters with local storage provisioner see its usage try out check out pvc-based example docs mons specify volumeclaimtemplate that points storage class while osds specify storageclassdeviceset with number devices provision template storage class used provision them enable ceph manager modules from cluster cr ceph manager pluggable interface that allows write custom modules particular use case rook now capable enabling any known ceph module this can done with help new cephcluster config mgr modules - name pg autoscaler enabled true this example are enabling pg autoscaler module see ceph official documentation full list modules upgrade maintenance improvements there are several improvements area upgrades first during rook upgrade either rook ceph version rook will wait each daemon healthy before upgrading next daemon this makes overall ceph upgrade safer more line with what ceph core team recommends next area improvements found when need service upgrade your k8s cluster have implemented pod disruption budgets all ceph daemons that will used when draining nodes maintenance this scenario depending which type daemon running selected machine drain rook will set pod disruption budget account availability needs each ceph daemon related note there are machine disruption budgets openshift clusters this works with machine-api controller which might send fencing request unhealthy node such event machine disruption budget enforces that only one ceph node can fenced particular time once that machine fenced rook waits ceph pgs settle will unlock machine disruption budget allow fencing other nodes enable these features handle upgrade see disruptionmanagement property cluster cr documentation osd configuration improvements number improvements have been made way that osds can configured expose more capabilities ceph-volume among these changes are included metadata device can specified per individual device desired instead only per node deviceclass property can specified per device indicate class storage configured crush map metadatadevice can specified explicitly instead relying system guessing which device use requires nautilus 14 2 1 newer placement improvements several improvements were made better integrate topologies k8s clusters into ceph topology particular rook will look zone region labels k8s nodes they are found mons will automatically spread across different zones osds will add zones crush hierarchy improve failure domain spread see topologyaware setting cluster cr under covers another placement improvement new implementation placing mons nodes cluster previously rook implemented its own scheduler decide which nodes place mons based desired node affinity tolerations specified cluster cr now removed all that custom scheduling code are using kubernetes scheduler place mons us see mon quot canary quot pods your cluster this their sole purpose within moments they will replaced by mon daemon pods that are scheduled same nodes less code means better scheduling conclusion big thanks ceph team many other community members all improvements this release truly this greatest set ceph features ever delivered rook release let celebrate this achievement look forward bright future continued improvements co-author ébastien han

performance updates including improved accounting omap key value object data by pool improved cache memory management reduced allocation unit size ssd devices note that by default first time each osd title: Introducing Cephadm
author: sage
content: wide variety ceph deployment tools have emerged over years with aim making ceph easier install manage most these have leveraged existing tools like ansible puppet salt bringing with them existing ecosystem users opportunity align with existing investment by organization particular tool result however ceph community investment been fragmented across many different efforts new users are faced with difficult choice tool when starting out attempts simplify experience integration with ceph itself been difficult like many others personally stuck with dated ceph-deploy tool which benefit being extremely simple use understand least someone familiar with ceph nice property requiring initial investment installing learning another tool these days ceph-deploy longer maintained however doesn t even work with some newer distros like rhel centos 8 most importantly however none these tools done great job solving core problem making ceph very easy install new user making ceph cluster easy maintain over time through seamless integration with ceph cli gui new orchestrator api first introduced ceph nautilus provide generic way ceph-- cli dashboard-- interact with its deployment environment whether rook ceph-ansible deepsea only with octopus this reached level maturity where providing meaningful abstraction across multiple backends rook kubernetes environments cephadm everyone else enter cephadm goal cephadm provide fully-featured robust well-maintained install management layer that can used anyone that running ceph kubernetes goals set out with include deploy all components containers using containers simplifies dependency management packaging burden across different distributions still building rpm deb packages course more users transition cephadm rook container builds fewer os-specific bugs see tight integration with orchestrator api ceph orchestrator interface evolved extensively during development cephadm order match implementation cleanly abstract slightly different functionality present rook end result something that looks feels acts like part ceph dependency management tools systems like salt ansible are great when deployed scale across large organization making ceph depend such tool means there one more piece software users learn more importantly resulting deployment ends being much more complicated harder debug most significantly slower than something that purpose-built managing just ceph minimal os dependencies cephadm requires python 3 lvm container runtime--either podman docker any modern linux distro will isolate clusters from each other supporting multiple ceph clusters coexisting same host historically been niche scenario does come having robust generic way isolate clusters from each other makes testing redeploying clusters safe natural process both developers users automated upgrades once ceph quot owns quot its own deployment can take responsibility upgrading ceph safe automated fashion title: Automatic CephFS Recovery after Blacklisting
author: jtlayton
content: linux kernel cephfs client gained ability automatically recover access cluster after blacklisting unblacklisting event cephfs relies heavily delegating recallable stateful objects represented by file capabilities dentries etc clients attain good performance this allows clients effectively cache granular information about filesystem performance forward progress also relies client return that state timely fashion when revoked by mds certain cases client can fail return its state back mds long time this could due bug client server loss connectivity between them this situation client can end blacklisted aka evicted by mds with all its state forcibly revoked once problem been solved administrator can remove client from blacklist past client needed -mount filesystem order recover which disruptive some applications starting v5 4 linux client accepts new recover session mount option default recover session which preserves historical behavior mount option recover session clean specified then client will attempt reconnect mds once blacklisting been cleared workload that all reads that doesn t involve file locking recovery should seamless can also used writeable mounts with file locking well client must take steps protect data integrity clients that weren t blacklisted ensure that its caches are coherent this situation any data metadata that written cache yet flushed out will dropped writeback errors will recorded against those inodes causing error returned when fsync called one its file descriptors file descriptors that are associated with files which any file locks were held will return errors any read write attempt against them all them must closed before any reads writes will again allowed general this option should used by most clients that have stable connections mds environments where connectivity may spotty availability more important than correctness admins may want consider enabling

title: Distributed Tracing using Jaeger in Ceph
author: Deepika Upadhyay
content: distributed systems like ceph can nightmare debug because they have single point failure address this have been working adding standard distributed tracing solution jaeger ceph jaeger distributed tracing open-source library project under cncf jaeger will provide more visibility into ceph distributed background processes help users identify abnormalities hence making ceph more transparent this blog presents opportunity learn about using tracing debugging ceph - perfect those looking identify performance bottlenecks latency optimization abnormalities distributed transactions are happy announce initial support jaeger pacific release ceph how does work jaeger tracing backend along with opentracing api provides ready- -use tracing services distributed systems becoming widely used de facto standard because its simplicity jaeger responsible collection spans these spans are made with use smart pointers they include timestamp traceid other meta info like specific tag log associated with span uniquely identified across distributed system these are then correlated generate visualizations trace lifetime request credits jaeger documentation let try out let take look into tracing core functions involved ceph input-output transactions please skip next section have jaeger backend set working with ceph information how set please refer documentation https docs ceph com en latest dev developer guide jaegertracing deploying jaeger services are going use vstart getting started with tracing this please ensure have ceph compiled with with jaeger deployed jaeger backend services - deploy jaeger backend service using vstart development cluster just need pass --jaeger option src vstart sh --jaeger by following above steps should able set all jaeger services access jaegerui http localhost 16686 read more https www jaegertracing io docs 1 20 getting-started all- -one jaegerui http localhost 16686 some reason are able access jaegerui retry manually running jaeger services using docker run -d --name jaeger -e collector zipkin http port 9411 -p 5775 5775 udp -p 6831 6831 udp -p 6832 6832 udp -p 5778 5778 -p 16686 16686 -p 14268 14268 -p 14250 14250 -p 9411 9411 jaegertracing all- -one 1 20 tracing core services now that have jaeger services running let take look into ceph core services tracing ceph currently can trace operations osd o path demonstrating here perform simple write operation which are using rados bench write can use any other available write interface your choice ideepika vossi03 build bin ceph osd pool create test create pool ideepika vossi03 build bin rados -p test bench 5 write -- -cleanup perform rados bench write 5 sec refreshing jaegerui http localhost 16686 should able see osd-services services field which specify traced osd processes lifetime request right below operations field which lists spans collected clicking which shall give traces containing see list traces gathered by our recent write operation x time -y duration graph with traces data points when click any traces should expand into all spans metadata stored them can store ceph metadata form tags logs while creating span seen below logs field carrying ceph relevant metadata there have your internal processes visualized exporting traces json these traces are portable they can converted into json output which can rendered other systems using jaegerui demo iframe allow accelerometer autoplay clipboard-write encrypted-media gyroscope picture- -picture allowfullscreen frameborder 0 height 405 src https www youtube com embed gvxlbl6vtvy title quick demo using jaegerui ceph width 720 what next this project still work progress however with orchestration right information real-time traces will having end- -end tracing which can make debugging much easier understanding internals ceph look forward improving observability ceph overall have some tasks lined improving tracing support extending tracing support clients rgw cephfs rbd integration with title: Ceph Pacific Usability: Advanced Installation
author: Paul Cuzner
content: starting with ceph octopus release ceph provides its own configuration management control plane form mgr orchestrator framework this feature covers around 90 configuration management requirements ceph why 100 well there are some tasks like preparing hosts purging cluster that need performed from outside cluster those tasks take look cephadm-ansible ceph-salt installation other hand completely covered by orchestrator first bit background orchestrator cephadm framework uses ssh under covers typically don t want ssh user account used by orchestrator module root account - need user account set each node that sudo privileges just like ansible controlled environment this account must able issue commands login without password this article using account called cephadmin will use ssh keys bootstrap node cephadmin account ceph using centos 8 stream vms with podman there are few niggles with podman support head over compatibility page double check versions available your host centos rhel deployments downgrading podman v3 0 covered this red hat bz 1946982 specifically this comment covering deploying configuring os worth reiterating 3 key requirements following packages must installed ssh python3 podman docker lvm2 chrony ntp ensure your hosts are resolvable by dns just easier that way optional ensure your sudo user account available ceph installation consists multi-step workflow that starts with bootstrap phase bootstrap process effectively brings orchestrator into play enabling all other hosts daemons deployed ceph components may now managed services governed by spec which introduces some default behaviours more that minute your first vm grab cephadm binary install docs are here with cephadm place cephadmin sudo user account configured each node ready bootstrap cluster cephadm --image myregistry 5000 ceph ceph v16 bootstrap --mon-ip 192 168 122 174 --ssh-private-key home cephadmin ssh id rsa --ssh-public-key home cephadmin ssh id rsa pub --ssh-user cephadmin --skip-monitoring-stack can see using --image override this allows us pull ceph container image from local registry instead reaching out docker hub everytime once bootstrap complete service specifications mon mgr daemons use count based placement policy this means that orchestrator will place these daemons anywhere meet number instances defined by count this normally fine purposes this post opting pedantic possible control everything that must modify default specs mon mgr through cephadm shell ceph root cs8-1 ceph orch apply mon --placement 1 ceph root cs8-1 ceph orch apply mgr --placement 1 now mon mgr services are limited single daemon which means can add more hosts have mon mgr pop where don t want them let add additional cluster hosts now root cs8-1 host cs8-2 cs8-3 cephadm shell -- ceph orch host add host done nb there are more options available when adding hosts check out docs more information here picture target environment aiming now can assemble single yaml file containing specs which determine desired state cluster root directory ceph daemon configurations var lib ceph this directory contains home directory which passed through your cephadm shell automatically which makes ideal place create our configuration files create file called cluster yaml that looks like this --- service type mon service id mon placement hosts - cs8-1 - cs8-2 - cs8-3 --- service type mgr service id mgr placement hosts - cs8-1 - cs8-2 --- service type osd service id default drive group placement host pattern quot quot data devices all true --- service type prometheus service id prometheus placement hosts - cs8-1 --- service type grafana service id grafana placement hosts - cs8-3 --- service type alertmanager service id alertmanager placement count 3 --- service type node-exporter service id node-exporter placement host pattern quot quot --- service type mds service id myfs placement hosts - cs8-2 - cs8-3 --- service type rgw service id rgw placement hosts - cs8-1 spec rgw frontend port 8080 this example declaring specific hosts service daemon placement could also use host labels orchestrator will use host labels guide daemon placement which can help make your configuration more tolerant change more information take look here now all that left give our desired state orchestrator act upon ceph root cs8-1 ceph orch apply - cluster yaml scheduled mon update scheduled mgr update scheduled osd default drive group update scheduled prometheus update scheduled grafana update scheduled alertmanager update scheduled node-exporter update scheduled mds cephfs update scheduled rgw rgw update can monitor your deployment through orchestrator ceph orch ls via ceph - progress updating grafana deployment 1 - gt 1 0s key thing remember about this service based approach that orchestrator continually reconciles against desired state defined by service specs past ceph releases may have had manually rerun your configuration management tool ensure things are where what they should with orchestrator this done once deployment complete there are couple post deployment steps that need take care before can declare victory start cephadm shell then follow these steps mgr prometheus module will need enabling prometheus server updating ceph root cs8-1 ceph mgr module enable prometheus ceph root cs8-1 ceph orch reconfig prometheus note this step temporary since there pull request underway handle this automagically although can see that mds daemons have been deployed where wanted them - there isn t pool corresponding filesystem yet this point ceph fs status will show both mds daemons standby mode complete configuration our myfs filesystem run this command from within cephadm shell ceph root cs8-1 ceph fs volume create myfs this will automatically create pools required myfs volume called cephfs myfs meta cephfs myfs data let leave block storage users out ceph root cs8-1 ceph osd pool create rbd replicated ceph root cs8-1 ceph osd pool application enable rbd rbd what have done ✔ have shiny new ceph pacific cluster defined over 3 hosts ✔ ceph services daemons have been hand placed specific hosts according our plan ✔ ceph gui enabled secured with https by default ✔ integrated monitoring alerting active prometheus alertmanager grafana ✔ storage can consumed over any protocol block file object

comparison bitmap screen captured various points test run its pixels are compared baseline bitmap comparison stage they iterate through each pixel pair then check color hex code same color codes are title: Caching mgr modules
author: Pere Diaz Bou
content: introduction while ago problems have been arising related scalability mgr daemon underlying tightly coupled daemon structure python modules like dashboard prometheus pg autoscaler orchestrators many more cluster data requested demand by modules every certain time order keep cluster status updated these modules example dashboard will periodically request health data updates daemon display cluster healthy there are instances data structures where scalability problem osds example can increase thousands therefore structures like osdmap will increase proportionally size thus increasing latency modules when they try retrieve newest data adding cache layer there have been talks what solve this problem agreed that cached mgr could help by decreasing latency large clusters which suffer from these problems grosso modo mgr modules are connected like can see daemon holds most maps cluster when something requested example get osd map will start transform osdmap pyobject with what call formatters pyformatter this instance caching pyobject difficult since would have make copy each python module used simpler approach where would transform structure json with jsonformatter where only have worry about serializing deserializing with json serialization place shared ttl cache between modules daemon added everything cached might seem diagram most problematic calls are serializing with json itself great improvement cache serialized object see 2 8x improvement with 3000 osds following line chart clear distinction made between current behaviour cache with json serialization this benchmarks were run by requesting osdmap 5000 times each number osds these are results blue dashed line represents improvement latency retrieve osdmap black line usual behaviour blue line results without caching json objects moreover cache available master quincy soon backported pacific can enabled by running ceph config set mgr mgr ttl cache expire seconds 10 that will set 10 seconds time live each cached object conclusion with disabled cache usual behaviour still faster nevertheless see clear improvement almost 3x larger clusters with cache enabled using simple serialization tool like json mgr daemon been unattended while lot improvements are needed have more scalable mgr this cache improvement that alleviates some workload there more work done addressing scalability debuggabilitty subinterpreters stay tuned

content: quincy 17th stable release ceph named after squidward quincy tentacles from spongebob squarepants this first stable release ceph quincy contents major changes from pacific upgrading from octopus pacific upgrading from pre-octopus releases like nautilus thank our contributors major changes from pacific general filestore been deprecated quincy bluestore ceph default object store ceph-mgr-modules-core debian package longer recommends ceph-mgr-rook ceph-mgr-rook depends python3-numpy which cannot imported different python sub-interpreters multiple times when version python3-numpy older than 1 19 because apt-get installs recommends packages by default ceph-mgr-rook always installed along with ceph-mgr debian package indirect dependency your workflow depends this behavior might want install ceph-mgr-rook separately device health metrics pool been renamed mgr now used common store all ceph-mgr modules after upgrading quincy device health metrics pool will renamed mgr existing clusters ceph pg dump command now prints three additional columns last scrub duration shows duration seconds last completed scrub scrub scheduling conveys whether pg scheduled scrubbed specified time whether queued scrubbing whether being scrubbed objects scrubbed shows number objects scrubbed pg after scrub begins health warning now reported require-osd-release flag set appropriate release after cluster upgrade leveldb support been removed with leveldb longer supported build option users -should- migrate their monitors osds rocksdb before upgrading quincy cephadm osd memory target autotune enabled by default which sets mgr cephadm autotune memory target ratio 0 7 total ram this unsuitable hyperconverged infrastructures hyperconverged ceph please refer documentation set mgr cephadm autotune memory target ratio 0 2 telemetry improved opt- flow that users can keep sharing same data even when new data collections are available new perf channel that collects various performance metrics now avaiable opt into with ceph telemetry ceph telemetry enable channel perf see sample report with ceph telemetry preview note that generating telemetry report with perf channel data might take few moments big clusters more details see https docs ceph com en quincy mgr telemetry mgr progress module disables pg recovery event by default since event expensive interrupted other services when there are osds being marked out from cluster however user can still enable this event anytime more detail see https docs ceph com en quincy mgr progress https tracker ceph com issues 55383 known issue mon cluster log to journald needs set false when mon cluster log to file set true continue log cluster log messages file after log rotation cephadm snmp support colocation daemons mgr mds rgw osd memory autotuning integration with new nfs mgr module ability zap osds they are removed cephadm agent increased performance scalability dashboard day 1 new quot initial challenges motivation --bulk flag before quincy some users who installed ceph out- - -box experienced performance issues from start by default autoscaler would begin every pool with minimum deprecated objectstore filestore 2016 began writing new objectstore called bluestore while filestore used existing filesystem store object data bluestore stores object data directly block device database writes them write-ahead-log also stores them -memory buffers called memtables this setting controls maximum number memtables that can accumulate memory note that this setting global across entire database instead applied separate database partitions called column families when bluestore originally written all data stored single column family now partition data across multiple column
