title: Ceph OSD CPU Scaling - Part 1
author: Mark Nelson (nhm)
content: introduction ceph does lot things very well never been known have incredibly low resource consumption takes work ensure that data consistent placed securely where needs go have multiple efforts underway optimize ceph data path reality that ceph historically needed quite bit cpu achieve high performance fast storage devices like nvme drives earlier this summer user approached our team with concerns about performance low cpu core counts they had been given recommendation that when using nvme drives 2 cores should allocated per osd that recommendation came with explanation why they decided purchase hardware though with only half nvme drive bays populated ie they had 4 cores available per osd performance acceptable that configuration user rightly concerned about what might happen when they fully populate their servers with nvme drives sadly had inform them that likely they would only see capacity increase performance increase by adding more drives original recommendation wasn t entirely without merit user isn t primarily concerned about performance small random io 2 cores per osd might good value proposition there are many benefits running ceph nvme drives beyond increasing small random io performance this user however small random io concern that precisely case when cpu resources are most important sadly this isn t first time this issue come there been lot confusion about topic 2 years ago updated upstream ceph documentation try provide better guidance this pr time our rough guidance before replication 1 core per 200-500 mb 1 core per 1000-3000 iops most important aspect here though iops performance this article will focus how ceph small random iops performance scales cpu resources increase cluster setup nodes 10 x dell poweredge r6515 cpu 1 x amd epyc 7742 64c 128t memory 128gib ddr4 network 1 x 100gbe mellanox connectx-6 nvme 6 x 4tb samsung pm983 os version centos stream release 8 ceph version pacific v16 2 9 built from source all nodes are located same juniper qfx5200 switch connected with single 100gbe qsfp28 link clusters were built fio tests were performed using cbt unless otherwise noted each node configured host 6 osds had 4 colocated fio processes using librbd engine important os level optimization intel systems setting tuned profile either quot latency-performance quot quot network-latency quot this primarily helps by avoiding latency spikes associated with cpu c p state transitions amd rome based systems appear sensitive this regard however tuned profile nevertheless set quot network-latency quot these tests testing setup cbt configured deploy ceph with couple modified settings versus stock primarily rbd cache disabled each osd given 8gb memory target msgr v1 used with cephx disabled more recent testing seen that msgr v2 with default cephx authentication appears perform similarly though enabling over- -wire encryption can have 30-40 performance penalty with similar higher cpu usage both servers clients fio configured first pre-fill rbd volumes with large writes followed by 3 iterations 4k random reads followed by 4k random writes iodepth 128 5 minutes each cbt allows osds wrapped with other programs environment variables numactl used control how many cores osds could utilize system initial tests were performed with single osd 1x replication multi-osd tests were performed with multiple osds 3x replcation single osd tests multi-osd clusters ceph places data determinsitically pseudo-random fashion there are likely hotspots given points time some osds will doing more work than others aggregate performance can suffer result ultimately overall cluster performance limited by performance slowest osd cluster testing against single osd eliminates this behavior further removes additional replication latency overhead ensuring that osd working peak efficiency testing single osd does represent what real cluster can does show how given osd can perform under optimal conditions first thing note here that performance increases by roughly 100 between 2 4 cores nearly linear improvement after 4 cores though gains begin slow going from 4 16 cores yields only another 100 with gains almost completely leveling 10 cores write performance scales higher though topping out around 350 14-16 allocated cores ceph osd really using all those cores these tests turns out that allocating more cores osds consistently improves performance 14-16 cores high core counts osds will consistently use all cores they are given this especially true reads more cores means higher performance efficiency degrades higher go iops per core used however remains relatively flat why this what are limits by default ceph osds have 80 threads per osd most important ones from resource consumption perspective are 16 osd worker threads 8 shards with 2 threads each 3 async messenger threads 1 bluestore key value thread 1 bluestore quot finisher quot thread rocksdb flush high priority compaction low priority background threads without getting too deep into details here save that later blog post practical maximum core usage stock osd probably around 23 cores highest usage achieved lab with stock thread counts over 5 minute period around 18-19 cores 4k random writes with limits imposed osd rocksdb write-ahead-log disabled why don t see that these tests likely answer that ceph simply can t keep all 16 worker threads busy all time ie there are short periods time when worker threads are waiting something before they can more work while osd average might use 6 8 cores may perform best when can burst 16 cores short periods time while other times may only need 3-4 cores this one scenario where running ceph bare metal may have advantages over running ceph containers vms hard core limit imposed 60 osd cluster tests trends that were observed single osd tests happen when full cluster deployed couple things immediately stand out when looking 60 osd cluster test results while curves look similar single osd tests performance tops out around 8-10 cores per osd reads about 12 cores per osd writes single osd test read write gains topped out roughly 200 350 respectively full cluster configuration gains topped out 100 250 simply looking osd 0 looks like osds larger cluster are utilizing even fewer cores random read tests simultaneously both iops per core allocated iops per core used numbers are also much lower write side 3x replication being used now able compare against single osd tests have look iops delievered by osds with replication factored even doing this per-core write performance also quite bit lower than single osd tests good news that estimates documentation appear fairly valid read side ceph delivering around 7500 iops per core used anywhere from 2400 8500 iops per core allocated depending how many cores are assigned osds write side ceph delivering around 3500 iops per core used anywhere from 1600 3900 iops per core allocated these numbers are little better than what claimed 2 years ago made further improvements recent quincy release single osd vs multi-osd nvme performance another question that comes fairly often how well ceph can utilize nvme drives usually this accompanied by benchmarks data being written read directly from locally attached drive user wants know why ceph slower despite being backed by more drives short answer that ceph indeed slower than just doing straight writes disk there are number reasons why some top ones latency introduced computing crush placement checksums encryption erasure coding network overhead etc processing data encode decode etc allocating copying moving data memory between threads even rocksdb ceph doesn t just write data writes out metadata about that data this can significant when performing small writes allowing threads go sleep when there work waking them when work arrives this done reduce cpu overhead during quiet periods hwoever can have significant impact performance when threads go sleep wake too quickly later blog post will talk about this more detail some these things are difficult improve without significant work ceph always going limited some extent by overhead communicating over network dealing with network stack though things like dpdk can help crush will always introduce some latency figure out where data lives there will always some level additional latency caused by crc32 encoding decoding etc having said that there very big performance difference between single osd multi-osd tests looking these charts little rough even though 60 osd cluster delivering around 2 million random read iops solitary osd capable delivering nearly 4 times per-nvme performance better efficiency write side things are little closer single osd still roughly 2 times faster per-nvme all lost however ceph quincy worked hard improve write path performance between improvements ceph quincy release selective rocksdb tuning achieved over 40 improvement 4k random write iops full 60 osd cluster vs stock ceph pacific installation find out how got these results see rocksdb tuning deep dive blog post here conclusion ultimately there still significant headroom achieve higher performance both cluster level inside osd future blog post will dig into some issues that are limiting performance low high core counts ideas regarding how ceph can further improved until then there are trade-offs when chosing how many cores assign osds that are backed by nvme drives 2-4 cores per osd ceph can mostly utilize all cores during small reads small writes adding additional cores even 16 per osd can increase performance with lower gains every core added efficiency per core used remains fairly constant osds become less consistent about fully utilizing all avaiable cores all times when higher core counts are assigned this effect upfront purchasing decisions also infrastructure decisions regarding things like power cooling even decisions about container vm resource utilization restrictions finally this post focused ceph pacific both efficiency top end performance ceph improved since then these curves likely look bit different quincy almost certainly will look different again reef these tests were also run fresh cluster may look same full cluster with significant amount aging hope however that this post least provided starting point how cpu resources impact ceph modern nvme drives thanks reading

title: Celebrating one exabyte of Ceph storage!
author: Yaarit Hatuka
content: are excited announce have reached 1 exabyte milestone ceph storage reported through our telemetry by more than 2 500 ceph clusters community background ceph telemetry introduced 2019 service that allows users phone home information about their deployments by opting- telemetry module generates anonymized reports according channels that are enabled sends them daily our backend our public telemetry dashboards display aggregated time series analysis about version adoption rates cluster storage capacity distribution storage capacity by version more since service launched see steady opt- increase from community installations here can see breakdown total storage capacity by version over past four years make your voice heard addition mailing lists that serve great communication channel when looking any feedback from community telemetry excellent resource developers that helps answer questions about how ceph used example when considering when deprecate filestore telemetry data helped understanding how commonly being deployed vs bluestore across versions here what telemetry tells us about osd count by objectstore version by looking real data from real clusters can make educated decisions about continuation support features clusters that phone home make their voice heard when look answers privacy telemetry reports are anonymized contain sensitive information like host pool object names fsid cluster reported ips are stored see sample report quincy later releases with ceph telemetry preview-all prior releases with ceph telemetry show-all leaderboard users who are opted- consists 6 nodes with 2 4tb firecuda nvme drives each they wanted know anyone would mind benchmarking similar setup report results here clyso are actively working improving ceph code achieve higher performance have our own tests configurations evaluating our changes code just happens that one places our work upstream ceph community performance lab appears good match testing this user request decided sit down couple hours give try u dividedbypi one our friends over 45drives com wrote that they are also going give shot report results their youtube channel coming weeks figure this could fun way get results from multiple vendors let see what happens acknowledgements first thank clyso funding this work benefit ceph community thank well ibm red hat samsung providing upstream ceph community with hardware used this testing thank all ceph developers that have worked tirelessly make ceph great finally thank u nnaz reaching out driving some new ceph benchmarking user setup user indicated original reddit post this article that they have 6 nodes that each have 2 4tb seagate firecuda nvme drives 64gb memory they didn t mentioned what kind cpus networking they have both are potentially important this test conveniently they already had fio invocation mind that they wanted evaluate fio --randrepeat 1 --ioengine libaio --direct 1 --gtod reduce 1 --name test --filename test --bs 4k --iodepth 64 --size 150g --readwrite randrw --rwmixread 75 while don t have any firecuda drives upstream lab have nodes that have multiple 4tb samsung pm983 drives 128gb memory each cluster setup nodes 10 x dell poweredge r6515 cpu 1 x amd epyc 7742 64c 128t memory 128gib ddr4 network 1 x 100gbe mellanox connectx-6 nvme 6 x 4tb samsung pm983 os version centos stream release 8 ceph version 1 launched using cbt important os level optimization intel systems setting tuned profile either quot latency-performance quot quot network-latency quot this primarily helps by avoiding latency spikes associated with cpu c p state transitions amd rome based systems appear sensitive this regard have confirmed that tuned actually restricting c p state transitions however tuned profile nevertheless set quot network-latency quot these tests testing setup cbt configured deploy ceph with couple modified settings versus stock each osd given 8gb memory target which think reasonable given that user nodes have 64gb 2 osds kernel rbd volumes were used with msgr v1 cephx disabled fio configured first pre-fill rbd volume with large writes followed by user random read write test certain background processes such scrub deep scrub pg autoscaling pg balancing were disabled rbd pool with static 4096 pgs higher than typically recommended 3x replication used user only requested test with single fio volume with single 150gb file tested that requested order push cluster little harder also ran tests with 16 separate fio processes writing dedicated rbd volumes spread across 4 client nodes with 16gb file each match user fio settings support gtod reduce option had added cbt fio benchmark wrapper gtod reduce option can improve performance by dramatically reducing number gettimeofday 2 calls fio make also disables certain features such collection op latency information during test evaluate impact ran tests with gtod reduce both enabled disabled based results decided leave gtod reduce disabled that could report latency data well just aware that about 3-4 improvement can had by enabling this fio option other than that all other options were either available cbt already default fio example randrw rwmixread 75 procs per endpoint 1 osd ra 4096 log avg msec 100 cmd path usr local bin fio this resulted fio line that similar user with couple differences mostly related recording iops latency single client against this small 12 osd cluster reason wanted run multi-client tests well however showcase just how much headroom this little cluster when serving additional clients with same mixed workload 16 clients achieved over 500k random read around 170k random write iops with just 12 nvme backed osds mutli-client tests qunicy reef showed roughly 6 9 performance advantage over pacific respectively enabling gtod reduce improves performance by another 3-4 single multi client cpu usage common issue see clyso with pre-existing nvme backed ceph clusters that cpus are undersized nvme drives serve that single client workload each osd consuming roughly 3-4 amd epyc cores serve multi-client workload each osd consumes rouhgly 11-12 cores ie even with just 2 osds per node 24 core epyc processor needed each node achieve maximum performance with these drives faster drives may require even bigger faster processors what uses all this cpu previous blog post about ceph cpu scaling mentioned that there are 4 main consumers cpu name count osd worker threads 16 async messenger threads 3 bluestore kv sync thread 1 bluster quot finisher quot thread 1 some cases rocksdb compaction threads can also periodically use cpu resources bluestore kv sync thread can easily become bottleneck small random writes especially when using lower clocked cpus overall cpu consumption however primarily result work done osd worker async messenger threads this combination crc checks encoding decoding memory allocations etc single multi client cycles op edit previously reported cycles op title: Ceph Reef - 1 or 2 OSDs per NVMe?
author: Mark Nelson (nhm)
content: hello ceph community time again another blog post one most common questions gotten over years whether users should deploy multiple osds per flash drive this topic especially complicated because our advice changed over years back ceph nautilus era often recommended 2 even 4 osds per flash drive there were obvious significant performance advantages time when deploying multiple osds per flash device especially when using nvme drives during octopus pacific development cycles that started changing introduced several performance improvements osd bluestore code example here here that greatly improved per-osd performance pacific nearing completion ran variety tests determine whether our recommendation should change expected octopus pacific are significantly faster than nautilus also longer show consistent performance gain with 2 osds per nvme versus 1 some tests still showed some gains though others showed slight losses these tests however are fairly limited scope does availability cpu resources change results are there other advantages disadvantages terms performnace resource consumption finally continued improve osd bluestore code since pacific see similar behavior today read find out acknowledgements first thank clyso funding this work benefit ceph community thank well ibm red hat intel samsung providing upstream ceph community with hardware used this testing thank well all ceph developers that have worked tirelessly make ceph great finally special thank anthony d atri acting editor this document approving fixes within minutes thank your help anthony all work ceph docs cluster setup nodes 10 x dell poweredge r6515 cpu 1 x amd epyc 7742 64c 128t memory 128gib ddr4 network 1 x 100gbe mellanox connectx-6 nvme 6 x 4tb samsung pm983 os version centos stream release 8 ceph version reef v18 2 0 built from source 5 nodes were configured host osds 5 nodes were configured client nodes all nodes are located same juniper qfx5200 switch connected with single 100gbe qsfp28 link ceph deployed fio tests were launched using cbt important os level optimization intel systems setting tuned profile either quot latency-performance quot quot network-latency quot this primarily helps by avoiding latency spikes associated with cpu c p state transitions amd rome based systems appear sensitive this regard have confirmed that tuned actually restricting c p state transitions amd processors tuned profile nevertheless set quot network-latency quot these tests testing setup cbt configured deploy ceph with several modified settings normally when testing ceph common think about number cores amount memory assigned each osd this testing however better think about how much cpu memory available per nvme drive each these systems can confortably support 16gb memory per nvme drive can scale 20 cpu threads per nvme maintain correct memory ratio osd memory target set 16gb 1 osd nvme case 8gb 2 osd nvme case numactl utilized control number cpu threads per osd osds were assigned two pools quot processors quot attempt scale both physical ht cores same time this processor physical core map generated using following bash one-liner paste lt cat proc cpuinfo grep quot core id quot lt cat proc cpuinfo grep quot processor quot sed blank g this showed that processors 0-63 corresponded physical cores processors 64-127 corresponded ht cores next numactl invoked utilize equal number physical ht processors which this article refer generally cpu threads instance assign osds pool 12 physical 12 ht cores total 24 cpu threads 4 threads per nvme osds were invoked thusly numactl --physcpubind 0-12 64-76 usr local bin ceph-osd tests were conducted with between 2 20 cpu threads per nvme drive fio configured first pre-fill rbd volume title: Ceph Reef Encryption Performance
author: Mark Nelson (nhm)
content: hello ceph community over past year been hearing from more more people who are interested using encryption with ceph don t know what kind performance impact expect today look both ceph -disk over- -wire encryption performance under couple different workloads our readers who may familiar what what these terms mean let review -disk encryption this also sometimes called encryption- -rest data encrypted when written persistent storage ceph this done using luks dm-crypt fully encrypt underlying block device that bluestore uses store data this fully encrypts all data stored ceph regardless wheter block object file data over- -wire encryption data encrypted when sent over network ceph this done by optionally enabling quot secure quot ms mode messenger version 2 clients ceph reef v18 2 0 ms secure mode utilizes 128-bit aes encryption encryption can also performed higher levels instance rgw can encrypt objects itself before sending them osds purposes this article however focusing rbd block performance will utilize two options listed above acknowledgments first thank clyso funding this work benefit ceph community thank well ibm red hat samsung providing upstream ceph community with hardware used this testing thank well all ceph developers who have worked tirelessly make ceph great finally special thank lee-ann pullar reviewing this article cluster setup nodes 10 x dell poweredge r6515 cpu 1 x amd epyc 7742 64c 128t memory 128gib ddr4 network 1 x 100gbe mellanox connectx-6 nvme 6 x 4tb samsung pm983 os version centos stream release 8 ceph version reef v18 2 0 built from source five nodes were configured host osds 5 nodes were configured client nodes all nodes are located same juniper qfx5200 switch connected with single 100gbe qsfp28 link ceph deployed fio tests were launched using cbt important os-level optimization intel systems setting tuned profile either quot latency-performance quot quot network-latency quot this primarily helps by avoiding latency spikes associated with cpu c p state transitions amd rome-based systems appear sensitive this regard have confirmed that tuned actually restricting c p state transitions amd processors tuned profile nevertheless set quot network-latency quot these tests testing setup cbt configured deploy ceph with several modified settings osds were assigned 16gb osd memory target guarantee high onode hit rate eliminate confounding performance impacts rbd cache disabled can hurt rather than help performance with osds backed by fast nvme drives secure mode msgr v2 enabled associated tests using following configuration options ms client mode secure ms cluster mode secure ms service mode secure ms mon client mode secure ms mon cluster mode secure ms mon service mode secure three sets tests were performed follows with cluster rebuilt between each set tests test set client processes io depth multi-client 10 fio processes per node 5 client nodes 128 per process single-client 1 fio process 1 client node 128 single-client sync 1 fio process 1 client node 1 osds were allowed use all cores nodes fio configured first pre-fill rbd volume with large writes followed by 4mb 4kb io tests 300 seconds each certain background processes such scrub deep scrub pg autoscaling pg balancing were disabled finally rbd pool with static 16384 pgs higher than typically recommended 3x replication used ceph luks tuning - 4mb ios ceph utilizes tool called luks encrypt block device that bluestore writes data there are several tuning options available that may help improve performance before diving into full set tests let look couple those options option description --perf-submit from crypt cpus disable offloading writes separate thread after encryption there are some situations where offloading write bios from encryption threads single thread degrades performance significantly default offload write bios same thread this option only relevant open action note this option available only low-level dm-crypt performance tuning use only need change default dm-crypt behavior needs kernel 4 0 later --sector-size set sector size use with disk encryption must power two range 512 - 4096 bytes default 512 bytes sectors this option available only luks2 mode --perf-no read workqueue--perf-no write workqueue bypass dm-crypt internal workqueue process read write requests synchronously this option only relevant open action note these options are available only low-level dm-crypt performance tuning use only need change default dm-crypt behavior needs kernel 5 9 later unfortunately kernel available centos stream 8 does support disabling read write workqueues thus were able test those options were however able test others did with initial focus multi-client test configuration io size configuration random reads random writes 4mb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4mb luks 98 31 54 72 4mb luks 4k sectors 98 56 52 67 4mb luks submit from crypt cpus 98 87 69 26 right out gate see that deploying osds luks only minor impact 4mb read performance major impact write performance this may slightly misleading since are network-limited read tests 11gb per node write tests however performance impact significant good news that using --perf submit from crypt cpus option mitigates some performance loss while couldn t test workqueue related performance options these tests there already pr ceph enable those options that been tested by josh baergen quot low load latency does appear affected much by these changes any differences don t really exceed our error bars quot quot high load that includes writes larger write more effective this change example osd node cpu usage dropped by almost half 4m sequential writes with substantial improvements latency p90 reads were two orders magnitude faster quot quot large block read-only loads might have had slightly worse latency hard tell certain quot one observations that josh made that workqueue options may help improve cpu usage while don t have those numbers let look cpu usage tests were able run during reads system cpu usage increases dramatically when luks utilized 2x cpu usage write tests overall cpu consumption appears similar even lower when performance taken into account cpu usage per io actually higher overall both read write tests utilizing 4k sector size luks appears result slight cpu usage drop ceph luks tuning - 4kb ios io size configuration random reads random writes 4kb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4kb luks 89 63 83 19 4kb luks 4k sectors 89 73 84 14 4kb luks submit from crypt cpus 89 35 83 04 performance impact 4kb random ios lower than larger 4mb ios 4kb reads suffered roughly 11-12 hit while writes took closer 20 hit aggregate cpu usage pretty close however system usage slightly higher while user usage lower correlated with lower performance when luks enabled general takeaway from these tests that --perf-submit from crypt cpus option can improve luks large write throughput likely worth using using remainder tests this article 4k sectors may also worth enabling devices that support them natively may help slightly improve cpu usage some cases multi-client tests - 4mb ios now that done some base-level testing luks let see what effect msgr v2 secure mode with same high concurrency workload io size configuration random reads random writes 4mb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4mb luks 98 87 69 26 4mb luks 4k sectors 94 90 87 43 4mb luks submit from crypt cpus 91 54 64 63 there additive overhead associated with enabling msgr v2 secure mode however bigger effect these tests from luks luks again results significant cpu usage overhead interestingly enabling secure messenger appears decrease system cpu consumption when using unencrypted block volumes ie luks entirely clear why this case though potentially slight reduction io workload hitting block layer might explain multi-client tests - 4kb ios io size configuration random reads random writes 4kb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4kb luks 89 35 83 04 4kb luks 4k sectors 100 25 94 96 4kb luks submit from crypt cpus 89 18 81 82 biggest effect again from luks biggest cpu usage effects also come from luks with slightly more system cpu slightly less user cpu association with lower performance one effects throwing much io this cluster that see high-latency events this case are actually pushing things little harder read side seeing worst cast latencies high 900ms good news that neither luks nor secure mode are having significant effect tail latency this saturation workload also know from our previous article ceph reef - 1 2 osds per nvme that putting multiple osds single nvme drive can significantly reduce tail latency expense higher resource consumption single-client tests - 4mb ios last year looked qemu kvm performance with msgr v2 aes encryption saw that encryption did have notable effect single-client performance ran several single-client tests here verify that still case reef io size configuration random reads random writes 4mb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4mb luks 98 80 96 65 4mb luks 4k sectors 87 51 73 84 4mb luks submit from crypt cpus 87 36 72 01 earlier multi-client tests observed that luks generally having biggest impact greatly increased cpu consumption large ios degraded performance large writes small random io these single-client large io workloads luks having very little impact enabling messenger encryption however having significant impact single-client performance while had much smaller impact overall cluster performance multi-client tests single-client tests - 4kb ios io size configuration random reads random writes 4kb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4kb luks 94 95 98 63 4kb luks 4k sectors 97 68 99 92 4kb luks submit from crypt cpus 96 54 99 49 impact both luks messenger-level encryption single-client small io however minimal usually only couple percent what about latency previous multi-client tests showed significant latency spikes due how hard were pushing osds these single-client tests latency far more even typical latency reads hovers right around 0 9ms with spikes exceeding 1 15ms write case more interesting latency still significantly lower typically around 1 5ms spikes were typically below 2 5ms though case where both -disk messenger level encryption used grew closer 3 5ms nature spikes appears cyclical over time however that pattern repeats across multiple tests completely rebuilt clusters this effect warrants additional investigation single-client tests - 4kb sync ios previous single-client tests still utilized high io depth allow many ios stay flight this allows multiple osds service ios concurrently improve performance some applications however require that ios handled sequentially one io must complete before next one can written read etcd journal good example this kind workload typically entirely latency-bound each io must complete least one round-trip network transfer along with whatever other overhead required servicing from disk io size configuration random reads random writes 4kb unencrypted 100 00 100 00 4kb luks 95 87 87 88 4kb luks 4k sectors 100 89 94 64 4kb luks submit from crypt cpus 95 29 86 31 biggest effect this case came from luks 4kb sync reads were slightly slower while 4kb sync writes showed larger degradation latency followed similar pattern with unencrypted results showing slightly faster response times than encrypted ones read latencies hovered around 0 13ms while write latencies hovered around 0 4ms with occasional spikes around 0 5ms conclusion this article looked ceph performance with both -disk over- -wire encryption variety different rbd test scenarios results those tests showcased several nuanced conclusions -disk encryption luks over- -wire encryption secure msgr 2x osd cpu usage large ios low effect cpu consumption high large write cluster impact low-moderate cluster impact moderate small io cluster impact high single-client large io impact low single-client impact high io depth low small sync io impact moderate small sync write impact partially mitigated with tuning general expect users see increased cpu consumption when using -disk encryption greatest impact expected large ios thankfully ceph typically uses more cpu during small io workloads customers who have designed their osd cpu specifications around iops requirements will likely suffer serious performance impact due lack cpu large writes see significant performance impact with -disk encryption however this can partially mitigated there -going work that may mitigate further -disk encryption also moderate effect small synchronous write performance over- -wire encryption biggest performance impact maximum single-client throughput does have small performance impact other cases well though effect usually minor always encourage test yourself see your findings match what saw here thank reading have any questions would like talk more about ceph performance please feel free reach out

title: v18.2.1 Reef released
author: Yuri Weinstein
content: this first backport release reef series first with debian packages debian bookworm recommend all users update this release notable changes rgw s3 multipart uploads using server-side encryption now replicate correctly multi-site deployment previously replicas such objects were corrupted decryption new command radosgw-admin bucket resync encrypted multipart can used identify these original multipart uploads lastmodified timestamp any identified object incremented by 1ns cause peer zones replicate again multi-site deployments that make any use server-side encryption recommended running this command against every bucket every zone after all zones have upgraded cephfs mds now evicts clients which are advancing their request tids transaction ids which causes large buildup session metadata resulting mds going read-only due rados operation exceeding size threshold mds session metadata threshold config controls maximum size that encoded session metadata can grow rgw new tools have been added radosgw-admin identifying correcting issues with versioned bucket indexes historical bugs with versioned bucket index transaction workflow made possible index accumulate extraneous quot book-keeping quot olh object logical head entries plain placeholder entries some specific scenarios where clients made concurrent requests referencing same object key likely that lot extra index entries would accumulate when significant number these entries are present single bucket index shard they can cause high bucket listing latencies lifecycle processing failures check whether versioned bucket unnecessary olh entries users can now run radosgw-admin bucket check olh --fix flag used extra entries will safely removed distinct issue from one described thus far also possible that some versioned buckets are maintaining extra unlinked objects that are listable from s3 swift apis these extra objects are typically result put requests that exited abnormally middle bucket index transaction - client would have received successful response bugs prior releases made these unlinked objects easy reproduce with any put request that made bucket that actively resharding besides extra space that these hidden unlinked objects consume there can another side effect certain scenarios caused by nature failure mode that produced them where client bucket that victim this bug may find object associated with key inconsistent state check whether versioned bucket unlinked entries users can now run radosgw-admin bucket check unlinked --fix flag used unlinked objects will safely removed finally third issue made possible versioned bucket index stats accounted inaccurately tooling recalculating versioned bucket stats also had bug previously capable fixing these inaccuracies this release resolves those issues users can now expect that existing radosgw-admin bucket check command will produce correct results recommend that users with versioned buckets author: Paul Cuzner (IBM),Gregory Orange (Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre)
content: from time time our friends over pawsey supercomputing research centre australia provide us with opportunity test ceph hardware that developers normally can t access pawsey supercomputing research centre provides integrated research solutions expertise computing infrastructure australian international researchers across numerous scientific domains pawsey uses ceph predominantly object storage with their acacia service providing tens petabytes ceph object storage acacia consists two production ceph clusters 11pb cluster supporting general research 27pb cluster dedicated radio astronomy this time one goals evaluate different deployment architecture osd hosts single socket 1u servers connected 60-drive external sas enclosures started by defining some initial questions help guide our testing efforts how well does osd drivespec cope when defining bespoke configurations required by dense nodes relatively small nvme dashboard features like led controls work with external enclosures are there any considerations when using vms rgw instances what performance like different ec profiles with simple get put workloads are there any deployment management issues with dense nodes how well does ceph dashboard deal with dense osd nodes can see these questions cover wide variety topics interests avoiding reader fatigue our observations will split into 3 blog posts covering installation management architecture validation performance deep dive scaling rgw instances overview short time here teaser environment some key performance results what did learn deployment note that prior 18 2 1 ceph-volume able consume multipath devices presented by external enclosure check your ceph version use device-mapper-multipath having issues our first challenge osd configuration defaults block db allocation are based capacity osd - our case 22tb however each osd node only had 4 x 1 6tb nvme drives - defaults couldn t used instead used spec file that explicitly defined space block db ratio osds nvme drives service type osd service id aio-hdds placement host pattern storage-13-09012 spec block db size 60g db slots 15 data devices rotational 1 db devices rotational 0 problem solved then our first hiccup found that osd deployment dense nodes can hit timeouts cephadm our case only happened twice can annoying there fix this reef which enables mgr cephadm default cephadm command timeout setting user defined this isn t planned land until 18 2 3 bear this mind planning use dense enclosures management with cluster deployed our focus switched management cluster with cli gui these were our focus areas how will high number osds daemons per node render ui how responsive will ui with over 1 500 osds how will disks represented given deployment based multipath devices will workflows like identify led control work with external hdd enclosure how enclosures affect normal operations like maintenance power cycles good news that general ui coped well with this number hosts osds led controls worked fine however there were couple stumbling blocks after osds were deployed device list dashboard didn t show hdds any more this inventory issue attributable ceph-volume itself which feeds gui also ceph orch device cli command tracker this 63862 switching between pages within osd view slow 3-4s can follow progress resolving this issue 56511 number ux enhancements were also raised tracker component description status 64171 ui includes expand collapse crush map view backlog 63864 cli show devices per node summary merged 63865 ui cpu thread count incorrectly reported merged mentioned earlier this hardware based 1u servers connected over sas 60 drive enclosure whilst sas connectivity with linux issue did find some related issues that would good bear mind boot time host reaches ready before enclosure lvm unable activate logical volumes used osds result awful lot osds down state ceph completely unaware enclosure hardware health during our power cycling tests two enclosures experienced faults ceph this manifested osds being offline root cause wasn t apparent until status lights enclosures were inspected finally during our data analysis hit issue where our monitoring reporting way higher put ops than those reported by warp tool making difficult reconcile ceph data with warp results tracker 65131 raised explore what going culprit identified multipart upload large objects warp client using multipart parallelism d expect ceph reporting each part upload separate put op which technically problem there isn t corresponding counter from rgw that represents overall completion put op - can t easily reconcile client rgw views architecture validation since osd nodes are single socket machines our starting strategy involved using virtual machines host rgw daemons leaving much cpu possible 60 osd daemons validating this design decision our next stop given that put workloads are generally more demanding used simple 4mb object workload litmus test chart below shows our initial disappointing results failing even deliver 2gibs throughput shows that there major bottleneck design ceph performance statistics revealed issues all which hardly surprising given hardware culprit wasn t ceph cpu network constraints hypervisors which were hosting rgw daemons looking osd cpu usage found that even though there were 60 daemons per host osd hosts were under any cpu pressure all next - prompt switch rgw collocation strategy relocating rgw daemons osd hosts also took opportunity collocate workload generators ceph index nodes now same same test delivered much more appropriate starting point can see adopting collocation strategy delivered 7x improvement put throughput this our first win will influence pawsey production deployment strategy our title: Simplifying RGW Multi-site Replication with Ceph Dashboard: Introducing the New 4-Step Wizard
author: Aashish Sharma
content: fast-evolving world object storage seamless data replication across clusters crucial ensuring data availability redundancy disaster recovery ceph this achieved through rados gateway rgw title: Improving Persistent Bucket Notifications Parallelism
author: Adarsh Ashokan
content: improving persistent bucket notifications parallelism problem hand persistent bucket notifications were first rolled out ceph pacific part rados gateway rgw project good background see existing blog post ceph io brief this post deals with improving performance persistent bucket notifications currently implementation doesn t fully leverage rados distributed capabilities each topic tied 2 phase commit queue implemented single rados object this design creates bottleneck sharded queue implementation allows notifications distributed across multiple rados objects enabling parallel writes via multiple osds -- example - suppose create 10 000 objects ceph bucket - current design all object created notifications are directed single queue object causing contention single osd - with sharded topic queues notifications are split across multiple queue objects multiple osds now handle writes parallel removing bottleneck --- -- what done old design each topic mapped one rados object deployments grow maintaining high availability resilient access s3-compatible endpoints becomes increasingly complex traditional load balancers are often centralized statically configured unaware adapt topology changes failures real time ceph tentacle introduces ingress concentrators per-node haproxy services deployed via cephadm each terminator fronts local pool object gateway rgw daemons allowing every ceph node act s3 ingress point this distributed design improves fault tolerance simplifies scaling by localizing traffic handling ingress concentrators alone don t provide dynamic
